title: Two Eyes Screening Event
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
Newark LGBTQ Center, Out Montclair and The Montclair Public Library invite you to an exclusive screening of Two Eyes, featuring Academy Award nominee Lily Gladstone.

In 19th century Montana, a painter's worldview is challenged by his Native American guide while exploring a new landscape. In 1970s California, a teenager’s life is shaken up by the arrival of an enigmatic transfer student. In present-day Wyoming, a trans youth attempts to work through his complex emotions with a nonbinary therapist. Two Eyes weaves together three distinct tales of queer identity into a single narrative exploring the power of human connection.

IN-PERSON SCREENING: Friday, October 9th at 7:00 p.m. EDT at the Montclair Library followed by a 45-minute live Zoom conversation with filmmaker Travis Fine. There is a suggested cash-only donation of $20.

Content Warning(s): Racially or Sexually Motivated Violence. This film does not have a formal rating, but overall themes are mature.

title: Whitewater Rafting Trip
description:
Coordinating with the release of the dam in the Lehigh River, this whitewater rafting trip is sure to be a blast. Perfect for all skill levels. This is a great way to GET YOUR FEET WET! 
 
How do I Sign-up?

Register here, or in the Student Recreation Center's main office, or over the phone (973-655-3340).

Saturday, October 10, 2026

title: Kill Goofy
location: Grove Street Theater, 130 Grove Street, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
Apricot Sky Productions’s new play, Kill Goofy by Livingston playwright Eric Alter, opens October 9 and plays for three weekends throught October 25. 
The story is simple on the surface. Two best friends, inseparable at thirteen, haven’t spoken in thirty years. One of them never left his childhood bedroom. His mother never left because someone had to take care of him. Then the other one comes back to town, and everyone in that house has been keeping the same secret. It’s a play about the things we never say to the people closest to us, and it sends people out the door talking. 
Please note the play deals with difficult subject matter and is recommended for ages 15 and up. The full synopsis and content advisory plus more information are at https://apricotskyproductions.com/killgoofy.

description: In the Spring of 2026, parishioner Ken Traficante began an informal once-a-month gathering of men at Holy Spirit Verona. title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Let's Walk!! Garret Mountain
description:
Let's Walk!!
Join me for the paved loop at Garret Mountain Reservation.

We will meet at the parking lot on the loop, turn right on Park Ave from Mountain Ave, lot is on the left. GPS Address for Garrett is 8 Mountain Ave Woodland Park.

Garret Mountain Reservation, located in both Woodland Park and Paterson, is one of Passaic County’s most frequented parks. The original landscape was designed by the famed Olmsted Brothers Firm. The 310 acres of recreational space sits more than 500 feet above sea level, with scenic views of Paterson and the New York City skyline. Lambert Castle and Lambert Tower, two of Passaic County’s historic sites, are also located within Garret Mountain Reservation.

Rain or extreme weather will cancel the event.

Collaborative walk with "Montclair Women Over 50."

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.

title: Olmsted Historic Walking Tour of Anderson Park
location: Anderson Park, 274 Bellevue Avenue, Montclair, 07043, United States
description:
Before Anderson Park existed, three houses and a fire station sat on the park property. Discover where they went and other surprising stories about how this Olmsted-designed Essex County park came to be created 120 years ago, how it shaped Upper Montclair, and how it led to the formation of other Montclair parks. On this illustrated tour, also learn about efforts to rejuvenate the landscape of this park, on the National Register of Historic Places. Handicap accessible. Meet in Anderson Park at the boulder at the park’s northeast entrance. Tour is from 10 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. Free. Call or check the Friends of Anderson Park Facebook page for weather updates. Sponsored by Friends of Anderson Park No rain date. Sponsored by Friends of Anderson Park, FriendsOfAndersonPark.com.

description:

Pollinator Meadow activities will focus on pathway installation and invasive species sweep and removal. Work is strenuous to moderate. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Please dress appropriately! Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots. please no bug spray. Wear sunscreen and a hat. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

description:
Join us for another Cookbook Swap!

And this time, we’re adding something delicious! You can bring a homemade baked good for fellow cookbook lovers to sample and enjoy. Please bring your baked good ready to serve—there will be no heating, reheating, or cooking of food at the event. Bringing a baked good is completely optional—you’re welcome to attend the cookbook swap and bake-off even if you don’t bring food.

If you plan to bring a baked good, please email adultprograms@montclairlibrary.org and let us know what you will be bringing. All baked goods must be nut-free.

Please note: Baked goods may contain other common allergens, and the library cannot guarantee an allergen-free environment or be responsible for allergic reactions or other food-related sensitivities. Please use your best judgment when sampling foods.

title: "Tales from Ovid" by Ted Hughes: Read-Aloud and Discussion of an Often Banned Poet NEW
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

The Roman poet Ovid has been upsetting censors for more than two thousand years. The emperor Augustus exiled Ovid from Rome shortly after the publication of his Metamorphoses. All Ovid's works were burned by Savonarola in the infamous "bonfire of the vanities" in 1497. And when Shakespeare's rival Christopher Marlowe translated Ovid a century later, the translation was set on fire again in the "Bishop's Ban." Then the U.S. Customs censored some of Ovid's work again in 1930.

To celebrate Banned Books Week, we'll be reading aloud and discussing "Tales from Ovid: 24 Passages from the Metamorphoses," an award-winning retelling by the longtime British poet laureate Ted Hughes. Come to class and hear for yourself what all fuss is about!

Dr. Melinda González is a Puerto Rican scholar and poet, who was born and raised in Newark, New Jersey, with ancestral home in the lush mountains of Moca, Puerto Rico. She is a socio-cultural anthropologist who focuses on environmental anthropology/disaster studies.

In  her book Curious Mind and Dancing Feet, we meet a young Puerto Rican Muslim girl with ADHD. She explains what life is like from her perspective; vibrant, exciting, colorful, and sometimes overwhelming.

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

title: Mount Vernon Trail Hike
description:

Join us for this point to point hike, the next in our 911 National Memorial Trail series, this with the Mt Vernon Trail being the subject. The official trail map shows this as a part of it, as a spur.
The trail is just over 17 miles, so it fits perfectly what we do, and after this one we'll start heading back toward NYC.
After meeting at the end point, we'll shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to our start point.
The Mt Vernon Trail is pretty straightforward, and follows the Potomac River the entire time, so it's really a great continuation from what we've already done with the C&O.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: Kill Goofy
location: Grove Street Theater, 130 Grove Street, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
Apricot Sky Productions’s new play, Kill Goofy by Livingston playwright Eric Alter, opens October 9 and plays for three weekends throught October 25. 
The story is simple on the surface. Two best friends, inseparable at thirteen, haven’t spoken in thirty years. One of them never left his childhood bedroom. His mother never left because someone had to take care of him. Then the other one comes back to town, and everyone in that house has been keeping the same secret. It’s a play about the things we never say to the people closest to us, and it sends people out the door talking. 
Please note the play deals with difficult subject matter and is recommended for ages 15 and up. The full synopsis and content advisory plus more information are at https://apricotskyproductions.com/killgoofy.

title: Hike with Dr. Kirk! 3-4 miles
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**Sunday, October 11, 3 - 5:30pm**

Free expert-led hike in South Mountain Reservation. Hike about 2-3 hours covering 3-4 miles at a modest pace over rocky trails with one long climb from the Rahway River up South Mountain. Focus on ecology and hydrology, led by Dr. Kirk Barrett, President of the Rahway Watershed Association and expert on local watershed issues. Good balance required. Children welcome. No dogs.

**Sponsored by South Mountain Conservancy and the Rahway River Watershed Association.**

Meet at Clipper Pavilion in South Mountain Reservation on Cherry Lane in West Orange (not at McLoone's).

Steady rain cancels. Advance registration required via https://www.eventbrite.com/o/rahway-river-watershed-association-29353243393 Email president@rahwayriver.org with questions.

Leader: Dr. Kirk Barrett, President of the Rahway River Watershed Association (RRWA) and expert on local watershed issues.

Please come to the starting point 10 minutes ahead of time so the hike can start promptly. Times are our best estimates; they can vary depending on conditions, and the size and pace of a group. If you have any questions, call the leader. **Temperatures above 90 degrees and steady rain cancels, but intermittent drizzle does not. You will *not* be notified.** **Bring water. title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

title: The Assembly of Lovers - Sufi Drum Circle
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Community drum and chant circle rooted in Sufi prayer. 
Meets every other Monday:  October 12, October 26, etc. 
Contribution: Sliding scale donation $20–$40 (no one will be turned away) 
This is a vibrant Community Drum and Chanting Circle, where we drum and chant from our hearts into the universe. This experience is open to absolutely everyone, regardless of background or belief system—all that’s required is an open heart and a willingness to connect through sound.  The term ‘lover’ in this context refers to seekers on the Sufi path who are longing for union with the divine energy.  You can think of this gathering as an expansion of the sema sufi meditations we used to offer.  It is looser in form, more focused on music, and does not necessarily involve whirling, although it is welcome if you are called to it. 
There is a rhythm older than thought. A pulse that moves beneath language, beneath belief, beneath the self that thinks it’s separate. The Mystics knew this. The Sufis practiced it in Majalis al-‘Ushshāq. The Assembly of Lovers. Not lovers of ideas. Not lovers of comfort. Lovers magnetized by the Beloved. Those who’ve tasted the Divine Honey and cannot forget. Whose hearts remember what the mind has been taught to ignore. This is a gathering for those who feel the pull. The Assembly of Lovers meets twice each month, a rhythm of remembrance. Each gathering deepens the last. The circle becomes a living pulse of devotion. If you have a drum, bring it. Medicine drums, frame drums, and ceremony drums are all welcome. The circle grows stronger when every heartbeat joins the rhythm. 
The Flow 
Opening (5 minutes)
We set intention. A short prayer to open the way. To align the heart toward what is Real. 
Chanting and Rhythm (30-40 minutes)
Using the Sufi Chants of the Heart as a guide (our vision is for the chants to grow to what the individuals in the circle are inspired to invoke), we share simple chants. The drum holds the pulse. The voice follows. The meanings are offered, not explained. 
Repetition is the technology. The heart softens through return. Through invoking the Divine until the one invoking dissolves. 
Silent Resting (5-10 minutes)
After the chanting, we sit. No guidance. No instruction. 
The echo of the words and rhythms settles. The heart rests in what was touched. 
Closing (5 minutes)
A prayer of Unity. Of Oneness. We complete the circle and return to silence. 
Gratitude for what was offered. For what was received. 
  
Who This Is For 
This is for those who’ve felt the pull and don’t know what to call it. 
For those tired of spiritual talk that never touches the ground. 
For those who suspect that the heart knows a language the mind cannot translate. 
For those who long. 
Not for something. Not for someone. 
Just longing itself. The flame that keeps you moving toward what you cannot name but cannot forget. 
Osama Janakat 
 
Osama studied Mathematics and Physics at Rutgers University, laying a foundation of analytical thinking that complements his creative pursuits. As a beat-maker and music producer, he explores the intriguing connections between music, philosophy, and spirituality. 
Born in Jordan with Circassian roots, Osama’s move to the US in 2004 sparked a journey of inner exploration and spiritual discovery. An avid student of the Sufi tradition, he continues to seek wisdom that bridges cultures and disciplines, finding harmony in the interplay of art and spirituality.

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

title: Finish Strong and Position Your Business for Growth
description:
Montclair Business Networking
Year-end has a way of sneaking up on business owners. You’re focused on finishing the year strong while budgets need attention, next year’s marketing plan is taking shape, staffing decisions are looming, and new growth goals are already on the table.
Before you start setting goals for 2027, there are some bigger questions worth asking:

* What drove your growth this year and where did you fall short?

* Does your team have the capacity and skills to support where you want to go?

* Are your marketing, financial, and operational plans working together toward the same goals?

Join us on October 13th and we’ll help you unpack it.
The panel discussion brings together experts in business growth, marketing, HR, and accounting to help you build a stronger foundation for the year ahead.
Topics include:

* 2026 Performance Review: What your financial results, marketing performance, and workforce health say about where your business stands.

* 2027 Growth Planning: Marketing, financial, and workforce decisions to make now as you set your goals for the new year.

* Execution Readiness: The people, processes, systems, and financial foundation you need in place to carry out your plan.

Who Should Attend?

* Business owners and entrepreneurs

* CEOs and senior leaders

* Sales and marketing leaders

* HR and people leaders

* Business development professionals

* Anyone responsible for helping their organization grow in 2027

Don’t wait until January to figure out what 2027 should look like. Use this session to take stock of where your business stands, identify what needs attention, and head into the new year ready to act.
Reserve your spot!

title: AMERICAN HIGHER EDUCATION: FOUNDATION OF DEMOCRACY, ENGINE OF INNOVATION
description:
American higher education evolved from an elite system training clergy into a vital pillar of our democracy and economic progress. While the nation's Founders recognized the essential link between education and self-governance, contemporary universities did not initially serve this broader public purpose.
The first dramatic shift came during the Civil War, when the Morrill Act of 1862 established land-grant universities with a public mission to train citizens in building the infrastructure and agricultural capacity of a developing nation. This democratic commitment expanded over the decades to include African Americans through the 1890 Morrill Act and to train educators via normal schools, like Montclair, at the turn of the century. Following World War II, the "Endless Frontier" report permanently linked university research with national security and industrial strength. This model, combined with the GI Bill's massive expansion of student access and the Bayh-Dole Act's incentives for commercializing intellectual property, established higher education as the primary engine of modern innovation.
Today, universities sit at the center of critical national policy, where federal investments simultaneously ensure democratic access through student aid and drive advanced economic initiatives. With many questioning the value of higher education, this lecture provides analysis of the current institutional landscape set in its historical context.

Hosted by: Campus Activities, Civic & Voter Engagement

title: Crane's Mill:  The Story Behind the Name
location: West Caldwell - Community Meeting Room, West Caldwell Public Library
description:
Join local historian Bob Williams on Tuesday, October 13 at 6:30 p.m. at the West Caldwell Public Library for a fascinating look at the history of Crane’s Mill and its connection to West Caldwell.

The story has a personal connection for Williams. When he was just 15 years old, he purchased a collection of historic ledgers from Crane’s Sawmill in West Caldwell. By then, the mill had already been dismantled and moved to Allaire Village in South Jersey for reconstruction although it was never rebuilt. The mill’s foundation ruins remained in West Caldwell for years, becoming a favorite place for Williams to explore throughout his youth and into adulthood.

title: Open Book / Open Mind; Heather McGhee; "The Sum of Us." With Michelle Alexander.
location: Montclair - First Congregational Church of Montclair, Montclair Public Library
description:
What if we've been looking at opportunity in America all wrong? What if individual groups stopped trying to get a larger slice of the pie and worked together to create a bigger, better pie? 

Join the Montclair Public Library and Partners for Health Foundation for an inspiring conversation between Heather McGhee, an influential economic and public policy expert, and Michelle Alexander, a renowned civil rights lawyer and author. They'll be talking about "The Sum of Us: What Racism Costs Everyone and How We Can Prosper Together," McGhee's landmark New York Times bestseller from 2021 about how overcoming racism helps everyone, not just people of color, and how to move beyond the zero-sum vision of American opportunity.  

After the discussion, there will be a Q&A period, followed by signing with Watchung Booksellers. 

Thanks to the generosity of Partners for Health Foundation, free copies of “The Sum of Us” will be available to the first 50 guests to enter (who have not already received books in the Library’s community read). 

Join our community read, Montclair Reads "The Sum of Us," between June and October to get ready for this exceptional evening. Thanks to the generosity of Partners for Health, we'll be giving away free books to book clubs while supplies last. Click here for more details and to find out about other supporting programs. 

The event will take place at the First Congregational Church of Montclair, 40 S. Fullerton Avenue. Doors open at 6:30 p.m. The event is free but registration is required.

Open Book / Open Mind is sponsored by Montclair Public Library Foundation, Watchung Booksellers, Anonymous Dr. Alex and Doris Malaspina, David and Mary Lee Jones, and our individual Underwriters. We are also grateful for the generous support of our in-kind sponsors, First Congregational Church of Montclair, The George, and Amanti Vino. To join our Open Book / Open Mind Underwriters, click here.

title: Tuesday Open Studio Figure Drawing
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Every Tuesday, 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space | All skill levels welcome 
*Cover art by Ling Chen. 











Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. 
Each week a different model – usually nude, and sometimes clothed – serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say, observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. 
This has become a supportive community of seekers, artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. 
Each session features a variety of poses, from quick gesture sketches to longer, more detailed studies. Whether you’re looking to sharpen your technical abilities, loosen up your line work, or simply enjoy the meditative experience of drawing from life, this open studio is designed to support individual growth in a collaborative atmosphere. All skill levels are welcome – we’ve even had poets drop in and compose verses to the vibe in the room. 
Bring your preferred supplies – charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paint are all welcome. 
Basic drawing materials are available if you don’t have any, and the shop has drawing pads and supplies for sale. No formal instruction is provided, but peer feedback and self-guided exploration are always part of the mix. 
Good music. Good people. See you Tuesday. 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space. 
Tickets are set at a capacity of 12, but we accommodate up to 18 for those paying in cash. 











“The object isn’t to make art, its to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri

title: All In: The Fight for Democracy Film Screening & Civic Engagement Experience
description:
Democracy doesn't protect itself—it depends on informed, engaged citizens.
Join Civic and Voter Engagement, in collaboration with the African American Caucus, for a powerful screening of All In: The Fight for Democracy, the critically acclaimed documentary that examines the history and present-day reality of voter suppression in the United States. Featuring voting rights advocate Stacey Abrams, the film explores the historical barriers, systemic inequities, and ongoing challenges that continue to shape access to the ballot box and influence civic participation.
More than a documentary, this screening is an opportunity to deepen your understanding of the democratic process, reflect on the importance of protecting voting rights, and engage in meaningful dialogue about one of the most fundamental rights in our democracy.
Following the screening, participants are invited to stay for a facilitated discussion exploring the themes of the film, the significance of voting rights in today's political landscape, and the role each of us can play in strengthening our democracy through civic engagement. Whether you're new to these conversations or actively engaged in public life, this discussion offers a welcoming space to learn from one another, share perspectives, and consider how informed civic participation can create positive change.
Join us for:

A screening of the award-winning documentary All In: The Fight for Democracy
A facilitated discussion on the film's relevance to today's political climate
Meaningful conversation with fellow students, faculty, and staff
Free food and refreshments
Civic-themed giveaways
Resources to help you stay informed and engaged

This event is open to all students, faculty, and staff. Come for the film, stay for the conversation, and leave with a deeper understanding of the importance of civic participation and the power of every voice.
Good film. Great conversation. Free food. Giveaways. One important conversation about the future of our democracy.

Hosted by: Civic & Voter Engagement

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: New Jersey's 44th Annual Law School Day
description:
Are you thinking about applying to law school? Join us for our 44th Annual NJ Law School Day at Montclair State University! All NJ college students and alumni who are interested in applying to law school are welcome to attend!
At NJ Law School Day, you can speak with law school representatives from NJ, NY, and across the U.S. about what their programs have to offer and how you can prepare to be a strong law school candidate.  Whether you are new to the idea of applying to law school or preparing to apply this fall, this event is a great opportunity to learn and connect.

 
What to Expect from Law School Day:
1pm - 2pm - Law School Panel Discussion
- For this session, you will hear from a panel of law school representatives about what they look for when reviewing law school applications and how to become a strong law school candidate.
 
2 - 4pm - The Law School Fair
- This is your chance to meet face-to- face with law school representatives from NJ, NY, PA, MA and across the U.S., and ask questions about applying to law school!
- The list of law schools attending is growing! Current law schools attending include: American, Fordham, Villanova, Ohio State, Seton Hall, Rutgers, Drexel, Penn State, Pace, Syracuse, Cardozo, Utah, Maryland, West Virginia, Richmond, Pittsburgh, and many, many more.  
- You can see the full list of law schools attending once you RSVP on Handshake on or after September 1, 2026
 
3:30 - 4:30 PM - Speed Mentoring: Pathways to Public Service
- After learning what it takes to get into law school, stick around to connect directly with professionals who are doing the work.  
- Through fast-paced, small-group rotating conversations, you’ll discover real-world career paths, and get honest insights into public interest and public service work. Come listen, ask questions, grab a snack, and make connections that can kickstart your legal, public interest, or public service career.
 
How to Be Prepared for Law School Day:

Be ready to share information about you, your interests, and your goals!
Write down the questions you have about law schools and the process of applying to law school
Bring something to take notes
Dress to impress!  Business attire is recommended
Registration for Law School Day will open on September 1, 2026 on Handshake
Questions? Need law school advice? Email Chrysten Colacicco, Pre-Law Program Coordinator at MSU, at colaciccoc@montclair.edu

title: Women and Money Roundtable - How to Make Sense of Today's Financial Markets
description:
A virtual, lively, and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio. 


Julia Strayer and Liz Maccarone will lead a lively and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio.

This is a virtual program that takes place over Zoom. As the date approaches, you will receive an email with the Zoom link.

About the Presenters

Julia Strayer, CPWA®, CIMA®, CRPC® Senior Vice President, Wealth Management Advisor.  Prior to joining Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2000, Julia was a vice president and private banker for BankBoston’s Private Bank for 7 years, responsible for asset management and trust services. Previously, Julia worked in marketing for 9 years with Merrill. Julia has a BA from Ohio State University and an MBA from New York University’s Stern School of Business. Julia has appeared on the CNBC show “Power Lunch,” CBS “This Morning,” WGCH’s “Women in Business,” in addition to featured articles in USA Today.

Liz Maccarone, CRPC® Senior Financial Advisor.  Liz joined Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2012. Liz works closely with high-net-worth individuals and their families to create personalized and comprehensive strategies that support their goals, including investment management, retirement planning, liability management, and multigenerational planning. Liz values the importance of establishing and cultivating relationships with families including the next generation. Liz graduated from Fairfield University with a dual bachelor’s degree in Finance and Marketing. She began her career working at a boutique investment firm as a Business Development Associate, specializing in commodities and futures trading.

title: The Winding History of School Sports: A Unique American Invention NEW
description:
This is a paid Adult School class taking place at the Yogi Berra Museum. Click here to register.

Why do American schools build stadiums, award athletic scholarships, pay coaches extravagant salaries even as academic programs get cut, and turn teenagers into campus heroes - while most of the world keeps sports completely separate from education? This lively talk explores the surprising history behind the uniquely American idea of the "student-athlete". By comparing the US system with the European model of independent sports clubs, we'll uncover how this unusual partnership began, why it became so powerful, and what it means for education - and the futures - of young athletes today.

title: Wine Confidence 101
location: Montclair - Cornerstone Montclair, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Build your wine confidence in just four weeks. Whether you are new to wine or already a
connoisseur, this approachable course will give you the knowledge, tasting skills, and
vocabulary to enjoy wine more fully—and choose it more confidently.

Throughout this 4-week course, you will explore the world’s primary grape varieties and
discover the many styles of white, rosé, red, and sparkling wines. We will break down
the basics of viticulture and winemaking so you can understand how grapes, regions,
and production choices shape the flavors, aromas, body, and texture in every glass. You
will also learn what makes the major wine-producing countries distinctive and how to
recognize key differences among grape varieties and wine styles.

Each session includes guided tasting practice, from visual assessment through aroma,
flavor, structure, and finish, helping you evaluate wine and learn why you like or dislike
different wines. Durin the 4 weeks, we will taste 20–25 wines from around the world,
making this class both educational and delicious. By the end, you will feel more
comfortable ordering, buying, discussing, and enjoying wine in any setting.

THIS EVENT IS 21  Students will be required to show a government ID to the instructor
upon arriving at the first session.

title: Building Your Financial Roadmap: A Financial Wellness Series
location: Montclair Bellevue Ave Branch - First Floor, Montclair Bellevue Avenue Branch
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Take control of your financial future with this four-part financial wellness workshop series designed to help you build a stronger foundation for making informed money decisions. Each workshop focuses on a practical aspect of financial wellness, from understanding how money grows and creating a plan for where your money should go, to preparing your family and planning for retirement.

Whether you're just getting started, looking to strengthen your financial habits, or preparing for the future, you'll gain practical knowledge, useful tools, and actionable strategies you can apply to your own financial life.

Each week we'll answer one important question about your financial future:


	
	How does money grow?
	



	
	Where should my money go first?
	



	
	How do I prepare my family for the future?
	



	
	How do I prepare myself for retirement?
	


Whether you attend one workshop or the entire series, you'll leave with practical knowledge and actionable steps to help you make informed financial decisions.

These workshops are for educational purposes only and are intended to provide general financial education. They should not be considered individualized financial, legal, tax, or investment advice.

location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, instructor Rob Haas will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

title: The Space for Music - Jose Bevia Trio with special guest Sergio Albacete
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Wednesday, October 14 | doors open at 7:30, show starts at 8 pm | sliding scale tickets $25 – $30 
Co-hosted by Seed Artists 
The Space for Music with the Jose Bevia Trio and special guest Sergio Albacete, visiting from Spain. 
Jose Bevia on piano and keyboard, Ronen Itzik on drums, Peter Slavov on bass, and Sergio Albacete on saxophone. 
This program explores the intersections of Andalusian musical tradition, contemporary jazz and improvisation, tracing connections between Spain, the United States, and Cuba. Across the eight works, traditional melodies and rhythmic practices are reframed through contemporary harmony, metric exploration, and spontaneous improvisation. 
The concert opens with Mononas, Sergio Albacete’s reharmonization of a traditional melody from Villanueva de la Reina in Jaén, Andalusia. Characterized by its distinctive major-key sonority and an unchanging melodic structure, the piece demonstrates how a traditional folk idiom can acquire new harmonic dimensions while retaining its essential identity. 
The Smell of the Sunshine, by José Beviá, shifts the focus to the Finger Lakes region of New York. Inspired by the light, landscape, and tranquility of Cayuga Lake, the composition combines influences from Ahmad Jamal, Bill Evans, and Bob Mintzer with unexpected metric shifts and evolving thematic material. 
In Tangos de Cazorla, Albacete draws on Andalusian folk traditions preserved in the mountainous regions of Cazorla and Segura. Incorporating the rhythms of tientos and tangos with the Andalusian cadence, the arrangement later engages with the harmonic language of John Coltrane, creating a dialogue between Andalusian tradition and American jazz. 
Nico-Lico, by José Beviá, explores the relationship between composition and improvisation. Influenced by post-bop, Latin music, and contemporary compositional practices, the work allows the soloist to shape the tempo and rhythmic flow, making time itself an element of musical interaction. Written and improvised passages gradually merge into a unified formal process. 
Eunidenserías, by Sergio Albacete, offers a contemporary perspective on the bulerías. Traditional flamenco rhythmic and melodic gestures encounter the metric and rhythmic concepts of modern jazz, particularly those associated with musicians such as Ari Hoenig. 
Sedona Valley, by José Beviá, is inspired by the dramatic landscapes of Sedona and the Grand Canyon. The composition translates the immense scale, vivid colors, and geological beauty of the American Southwest into a musical reflection on place and memory. 
Nana del Caballo Grande, based on the music of Camarón de la Isla and arranged by Sergio Albacete, revisits one of the defining works of La Leyenda del Tiempo. The arrangement connects Camarón’s modern flamenco language with the historic form of the caña, linking ancient Andalusian song traditions with the transformative aesthetics of 20th-century flamenco. 
The program concludes with La Guarida, José Beviá’s tribute to Cuban music and to a deeply personal moment in Havana. Inspired by a piano lesson with a Cuban musician, the composition develops a montuno as a recurring subject, transforming it through successive variations, improvisation, and bitonal passages. The piece ultimately becomes both a musical exploration and a personal narrative, named for the Havana restaurant where Beviá proposed to his wife, Maggie. 
BYOB is welcome, some light refreshments will be offered. 
  
Sergio Albacete is a Spanish multi-instrumentalist, composer, arranger, and researcher with a
distinguished 30-year career. He holds advanced studies in classical saxophone and a Master’s
Degree in Jazz Performance from Musikene. He has performed and conducted Big Bands for 25
years and has been a tenured faculty member at the “Ramón Garay” Professional Conservatory
since 2004.
Albacete has collaborated and performed with internationally renowned musicians including
Barry Harris, Eric Alexander, Kurt Elling, Lee Konitz, Jerry Bergonzi, Perico Sambeat, Marco
Mezquida, Enrique Morente, and Claude Delangle. His career has taken him across Spain,
Portugal, Denmark, Germany, the United States, and the United Arab Emirates, and he has
participated in more than 30 album recordings.
His distinctions include the 2015 Culture Award from the City Council of Torredelcampo, Best
Album at the 2016 Jaén Music Awards, the 2018 Musical Excellence Award from Diario Jaén, the
2024 Jaén Public Employment Award, and the 2026 Grajo Award for Modern Music and Other
Styles.

title: Prompting for Data People: Getting Real Work Out of Copilot and Claude
description:
Cloud Data Driven
Most data professionals have tried an AI assistant, got a mediocre answer, and quietly went back to Stack Overflow. The difference between mediocre and magical is the prompt — and prompting for DATA work has its own rules: schemas matter, sample rows matter, constraints matter, and “show your reasoning” beats “give me code”.

In this hands-on session I share the prompting method I use daily with GitHub Copilot and Claude across T-SQL, DAX and Python: how to give context without pasting your whole database, how to make the AI ask YOU clarifying questions, how to iterate instead of restarting, and how to spot the confident nonsense. Live demos throughout, including at least one glorious AI failure and how to catch it. Works with any assistant your company allows.

Attendees will learn a practical, repeatable prompting method for data work with GitHub Copilot and Claude: giving schema and sample-row context without oversharing, making the AI ask clarifying questions, iterating instead of restarting, and reviewing AI-generated T-SQL/DAX/Python before trusting it. They leave with a reusable prompt template and a checklist for reviewing AI-generated code.

title: ACC Teach-In: Modern US Foreign Interventionism, Iran, and You!
description:
Drawing inspiration from the mid-1960s anti-war movement, this teach-in will be an action-based educational forum concerning modern US foreign interventionism and its historical convergence with Iran during the Cold War. More specifically, it will focus on the rise of the postwar national security state and its first pivotal and consequential “win”: the 1953 Iranian coup d'état. It was the first "successful" overthrow of a democratically elected foreign leader by the CIA (and definitely not the last). It is a tale that is regularly expunged from conventional American history, yet it is vastly significant to both Iranian US history. This chapter elucidates, in part, why both nations find themselves where they are today. In addition, this teach-in will also highlight the determining role of big business, military keynesianism, and neocolonialism in shaping the confines of postwar U.S. foreign policy. This teach-in will conclude with a discussion on what this all means for the ongoing US-Israeli war against Iran, and what actionable acts can be done to end the conflict.

title: Tea & Tarot - A bookclub style discussion group
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Monthly Gathering | Thursday, October 15th | 7:00 PM – 8:30 PM | The Space | $25 
Calling all tarot lovers, both new and seasoned!  Join us for an intimate way of exploring the cards. 
What could be better than a cozy evening of warm tea and deep conversation? Join us for Tea & Tarot with Gina Devine—a monthly, book club-style discussion group created to deepen our connection with the archetypes of the tarot through community and shared insight. 
Rather than a formal class, this is a casual meet-up where we treat the tarot as a living text. Based on the psychological insights of Carl Jung, we will explore the Major Arcana not just as fortune-telling tools, but as mirrors of our own lives, rituals, and transformations. 
The Experience 
Each month, we open a new gateway of creative and spiritual exploration. Our time together includes: 

Archetypal Deep Dives: We’ll focus on a specific theme or set of cards each session, discussing their symbolism and how they show up in our modern world.
Collaborative Readings: A chance to pull cards for one another in a supportive, low-pressure environment.
Ritual & Connection: We’ll sip tea, share stories, and find common ground in the mysteries of the deck.
Intuitive Growth: Whether you’ve been reading for decades or just bought your first deck, you’ll leave with a deeper understanding of the “BodyGraph” of the tarot.

What to Bring 
To make the most of our evening, please bring the following if you can: 

Your Tarot Deck: Any deck you feel connected to.  If you don’t have any we have some available here to use.
Your Favorite Mug: We’ll provide a selection of teas, and don’t worry if you don’t bring your mug – we have those too!
A Notebook: For capturing insights, spreads, and “aha” moments.

Investment: $25 
Stay Connected: Sign up for the Soul Centric Tarot Newsletter here. 
Spaces are limited to keep our discussion intimate and impactful. Reserve your spot today and join the circle. 
Cover art by Sophie Bryant Funnell 
______________________________ 

Your Guide Gina Devine
Instagram: @gina.devine 

Gina Devine is an esoteric artist, intuitive tarot reader, writer, educator and guide. 
She has provided thousands of readings for people all over the world, and leads both protection and tarot workshops. Her approach to guidance is loving, grounded and human. Although she also teaches traditional tarot classes, her tea and tarot discussion group was birthed from the knowing that people are more inclined to to be in tune with the archetypes of the cards and the messages they bring when they are allowed space to enjoy the tarot in a more casual setting – instead of forcefully trying to memorize them. The same way we find joy in discussing a book in community, the cards also call for us to convene together around them. Her approach is philosophical, therapeutic and creative, and she is on a mission to guide people toward unearthing a more intimate and honest relationship with their inner knowing through the art of divination. You can find her services and more at soulcentrictarot.com

title: Compagnie Hervé KOUBI: Sol Invictus
description:
Run Time: 75 minutes, no intermission. 
A jubilant ritual full of love and light from the acclaimed French-Algerian ensemble Compagnie Hervé KOUBI. Named after the “invincible sun” deity, Sol Invictus upholds love as the guarantor of peace, that despite fracture, communion emerges as humanity’s saving grace. A vivid celebration of solidarity and the bonds that unite us, in Sol Invictus the sun will emerge victorious. The score includes a composition by Swedish composer Mikael Karlsson, with excerpts by Steve Reich and digital composer Maxime Bodson. 
“The dancers of Compagnie Hervé KOUBI could be mistaken for gods.” (The New Yorker) 
About Compagnie Hervé KOUBI: Absolutely unique and utterly original, this fearless, powerful company reigns from France, Algeria, and beyond. Combining contemporary and urban dance movements, capoeira, and martial arts with powerful imagery and inspired choreography, the dancers defy gravity.

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Entrepreneurship Bootcamp
location: Bloomfield - Conference Room, Bloomfield Public Library
description:
*** This is a free program, but you must register to attend. 

email: reference@bloomfield.bccls.org

call: 973-566-6200 ext. 215 ***

Thinking about starting a business—or wondering what it takes to move your idea to the next level? This two-day introductory entrepreneurship bootcamp provides a practical overview of the key areas every new entrepreneur should understand.

Presented by Jesse Bryant, Certified Business Consultant with the Small Business Administration (SBA), SCORE, and Veterans Business Outreach Center (VBOC), the program will cover the fundamentals of building a business, including financing options, sales and marketing strategies, intellectual property, choosing the right legal entity, business planning, and incorporating AI into business operations. Participants will also learn about revenue-readiness software and discover support programs, resources, and organizations available to help entrepreneurs launch and grow.

This program is designed for aspiring entrepreneurs, new business owners, veterans, and anyone interested in learning more about the process of turning a business idea into a sustainable venture. No prior business experience is required.

description:
The class is geared to beginners and those who seek a refresher in the topic.  Students will gain a basic understanding of the worksheet environment, tools for working with data, and resources for continued learning.

This is a hands-on class; students should be able to use the mouse and keyboard.  Students are welcome to bring a flash drive to save their work for review and practice.

Summary of Topics:

Class 1:  Worksheet basics using a budget - Learn elements of the worksheet, enter and edit budget data, perform calculations, create a pie chart.

Class 2:  Format a worksheet for an attractive, easily-readable on-screen presentation as well with the attributes needed for printing.

Class 3: Formulas & Functions – learn more about how to use formulas, and the wide array of built-in functions.  Includes the concepts of relative and absolute cell references, named ranges in formulas; and how to create and use a Table to streamline your work.  [After this class, students will be ready to work with Pivot Tables, an even more powerful way to work with data.]

description:
About the program

There aren't many fruits that are native to the United States. Cranberries are one of them. Before Europeans came, Native Americans used them for food, medicine, and dye. Since the 1800s, cranberries have been a big crop in New Jersey. This text discusses the background, significance, and growing of these sour berries in New Jersey. The text will also look at cranberry-based early American recipes.

About the presenter

Judith Krall-Russo has consistently had a passion for cuisine, especially the plentiful farming in her home state of New Jersey. She commenced her exploration of the customs and rituals surrounding this prevalent beverage three decades ago and has subsequently acquired qualifications as a tea expert from The Specialty Tea Institute of New York and The Tea School in Pomfret, Connecticut. She is likewise a specialist and scholar in the field of tea. Krall-Russo is currently engaged in the Gong Fu Chinese tea ceremony at The Tea Gallery and the Japanese tea ceremony at the Uresenke Chanoyo Center in New York City.

title: NJ Code & Coffee - Newark Tech Week edition
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus during Newark Tech Week!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

* your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,
* What you can help others with,
* What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

description:

We're a group of people who will start by hitting the ball around for the first 20-30 minutes and then will break up into 2-4 teams for two or three hours of CASUAL play.

If we have more than 20 people show up, we'll break up into three or four teams of 6 (Some may have 7, 8 or 9. Additional players just rotate into play). Games will be to 15 points. Rally scoring. Winner stays on (unless a team has won four straight).

We'll be heading outdoors to the hard court in Leonia off Overpeck County Pk Driveway in the Overpeck County Park.

\*\*\*After playing, we'll likely head to Tropical Juice Bar, an idea of regular attendee Kate, for a drink and snack. The juice and smoothie bar is located at 60 River St. in Hackensack. Feel free to join us or suggest another spot for a post-volleyball hangout. \*\*\*

There's no fee to play volleyball and nothing else you need to do besides show up. Come anytime!! All are welcome!!!

This is a CASUAL play. We're not in a league and are not here to analyze your form. Most of us are average at best, and some haven't played in months, maybe years, and just want to occasionally play again and hang out.

Directions: You can Google "Volleyball Court in Leonia" and it should come up. Or type 41 Willow Tree Road, Leonia, NJ 07605 into your GPS, but note that it's not on Willow Tree Road, just near it. Instead, turn onto Overpeck County Pk Driveway off Fort Lee Road (Degraw Avenue). It is past the tennis courts and near a basketball court and track. You can try Googling "Leonia High School" as well. That should help you find it. You can go to the back high school parking lot and then cross over the train tracks.

Please note. We don't have the court reserved. If it happens to be taken, we may play with those already occupying it, wait up to a half hour for the existing game to end, or try to relocate on the fly. It's certainly possible that we may have to cancel that day if we can't find a suitable spot. And if it's looking like it'll rain or snow, I'll make a call on whether to cancel around an hour ahead of the scheduled start time.

Please bring a ball and net if you have them for possible use during the game. Feel free to bring a speaker for music, or snacks and drinks for consumption during play.

If you have trouble finding the court or group, you can call or text Andy Milone at 201-234-9609. There is plenty of parking and an open bathroom at the park.

Hope you'll join us for our 22nd casual volleyball event. Questions or comments? You can message Andy on Meetup, or call/text him at 201-234-9609. Check out bowling, soccer, volleyball, tennis or one of our other activities at: www.meetup.com/north-jersey-bowling-soccer-volleyball

If interested in staying touch with group members or conversing about future events, feel free to inquire about our WhatsApp group chat.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: Brandywine Valley Happy Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
join us for this lovely point-to-point hike in Chester County, Pennsylvania, featuring more of the diverse trails and back roads in the vicinity of the Brandywine Creek.
After meeting at our endpoint, Shaw's Bridge Park, we will shuttle with as few cars as possible to our beginning Point near Downingtown to begin our 15 or 16 mile hike.
The first portion of this will be on the regular Brandywine Trail, and then we'll make our way up to Harmony Hill. between Harmony Hill, Starr Farm, and a couple of other Parks, we will cover. probably about 7 miles.
we'll make our way down to a few country roads and skip a piece of the Brandywine Trail that was not maintained from a previous hike, and then headed to the Stroud Preserve.
we'll watch the miles to determine how much we do there, and then make our way south a bit more on some back roads to Shaw's Bridge.
This will probably be the last hike in our Brandywine series for the season, and will head back when the weather gets warm again.
There are no stores of any kind on this hike, so everyone should come prepared with all the food and water they need for this one.
If needed, contact me at 9083438374

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

Tantra Date for Couples: Fall in Love
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Couples, 
This fall, slow down… and fall in love again. 
When the seasons change, we feel it in our bodies—cooler air, shorter days, a natural pull inward. It’s the perfect time to come home… to yourself and to each other. 
Most couples want more connection—more warmth, more affection, more real intimacy. But between busy schedules, stress, and “same-old” routines, it’s easy to drift into autopilot. And the truth is: no one ever taught us the simple skills that keep love alive. 
Welcome to a brand-new, transformational date experience designed to help you reconnect, reignite, and remember what brought you together in the first place. 
This isn’t talk therapy, and it’s not a lecture. It’s a guided, gentle, playful, deeply grounding experience where you’ll learn easy, practical tools to create closeness—tools you can use the very next day at home. 
I also weave in practical, science-backed relationship tools inspired by the world-renowned Gottman Institute— simple skills that help couples strengthen communication, build trust, and keep love alive. 
Whether you’re completely new to Tantra or you’ve attended our events before, this experience is entirely new and different—crafted to help you shed what’s been weighing you down and step into a fresh season of love. 
Together, you’ll be guided through simple embodied practices that strengthen: 
– Emotional connection (feeling seen, safe, and understood) 
– Communication (without pressure or “doing it wrong”) 
– Trust + presence (getting out of your head and back into your hearts and bodies) 
– Everyday intimacy (small moments that change everything) 
By the end of our time together, you’ll leave feeling more grounded, open, connected, and genuinely close—and you’ll have a set of simple connection rituals you can bring into your relationship again and again… all season long. 
PRIVATE COUPLES COACHING: If you’re going through challenges in your relationship or you’d prefer a private, personalized experience—private couples coaching is available.  Text Olga at (862) 251-2444 to schedule a free discovery zoom call to see how we can work together.

BONUS: Couples Zoom Coaching Call with me. Schedule it after the event to help you integrate what you learned, troubleshoot what gets in the way, and keep your relationship moving forward together. 
FIRST TIMERS WELCOME CALL with the organizer is required to attend. Please TEXT Olga before ordering tickets. (862) 251-2444. Once we’ve spoken you are ‘IN’ and may attend all future events. Attendance is at the discretion of the organizer.

REFRESHMENTS: Healthy refreshments are provided halfway thought the event. 
PLEASE REFRAIN from wearing scented products to respect those with chemical sensitivities.

title: Memory Café - A Dementia-Friendly Social Gathering
description:
For adults with dementia and their caregivers, this event offers a welcoming, safe, calming space for socializing, music, art and reminiscing every month.


A “Memory Café” is a dementia-friendly social gathering for individuals with early-stage memory loss or mild cognitive decline and their care givers.

The meetings will be held in a safe and comfortable environment where people can interact and socialize with others having similar experiences. At the gatherings participants can get support in a non-judgmental setting, while enjoying the benefits of music for the brain.

The meetings will be run by Lisy Espindola, LCSW and Kim McLennon, MSW and music therapist. Lunch and/or snacks will be served.

This is a joint program between Lifelong Montclair at the Township of Montclair and the Montclair Public Library.

Attendance is free but registration is required. Questions? Call 973-744-3278.

To stay informed, sign up for one or all of our eNewsletters, click here.

Photographs may be taken during our programs and events for promotional purposes such as social media and e-newsletters. If you do not wish to have your photograph taken please let us know before the event.

location: Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:

The presentations combine music, maps, musicians, narratives and memories!

Paul will highlight his travels to Memphis, Tenn.: Hamburg, Germany; Hawthorne, Calif.; Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; Central Avenue in Los Angeles; Abbey Road in London; La Caverne de la Huchette in Paris; Clarksdale, Miss.; West 70th Street in New York; S. Michigan Avenue in Chicago, Il; W. Rampart Street in New Orleans; Tupelo, Miss, Grand Boulevard in Detroit; Cleveland; Liverpool, England; the 9th Ward of New Orleans, 9137 S. Figueroa in Los Angeles--and more.

title: Affordable College Solutions NOW ON ZOOM
description:
Register HERE

Join us for the special ZOOM presentation of the "Cracking the Code: Affordable College Solutions" seminar.  

It doesn't matter how old your kids are...now is the time to learn how to finance college!

This program will be presented by a nationally recognized Certified College Funding Specialist who has
been invited to speak to families and professionals by more than 65 organizations nationwide. She has also
provided continuing education to over 40,000 CPAs across the country on strategies to help make college
more affordable.
Designed for parents with children of all ages—from newborn through college—this engaging and informative
session addresses one of the most stressful financial challenges families face today: how to pay for college
without jeopardizing long-term financial goals and retirement. Even higher-income families with substantial
resources can feel overwhelmed by the tremendous cost of school and seek guidance to navigate the quickly
evolving college process to secure discounts and preserve their wealth.
A featured focus of the presentation is recent legislation often referred to as “The Big Beautiful Bill,” and
what it means for college savings, financial aid, and affordability. The presenter will explain these changes in a
clear, practical, and easy-to-understand way.
Participants will also learn about:
● How to secure a quality education without overpaying for college
● Understanding the financial aid landscape: FAFSA and CSS Profiles, need-based and merit-based aid,
athletic and private scholarships
● Student Aid Index (SAI): How it’s calculated and directly impacts your family’s financial aid eligibility
● Pros and Cons of Diverse College Savings Vehicles - a look at 529 plans as well as alternative savings
strategies and determining how to choose what’s right for your family
● How to reduce student loan debt and plan for repayment without sacrificing your family’s future
● Strategies to recapture out-of-pocket college expenses
● Positioning families to maximize college discounts: Practical strategies—even for higher-income
households—to unlock savings opportunities
Participants will gain valuable insights, expert guidance, and creative strategies to help make smarter college
funding decisions while protecting the ability to retire comfortably. This program is designed to simplify and
demystify the college funding process, empowering families to reduce costs and avoid unnecessary debt.
Whether your child was just born or is approaching college decisions, this program will provide clarity,
confidence, and practical guidance you can use right away.



PRESENTED BY: Jodi Bloom, MBA
Certified College Funding Specialist
Founder and College Planning Expert

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Building Your Financial Roadmap: A Financial Wellness Series
location: Montclair Bellevue Ave Branch - First Floor, Montclair Bellevue Avenue Branch
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Take control of your financial future with this four-part financial wellness workshop series designed to help you build a stronger foundation for making informed money decisions. Each workshop focuses on a practical aspect of financial wellness, from understanding how money grows and creating a plan for where your money should go, to preparing your family and planning for retirement.

Whether you're just getting started, looking to strengthen your financial habits, or preparing for the future, you'll gain practical knowledge, useful tools, and actionable strategies you can apply to your own financial life.

Each week we'll answer one important question about your financial future:


	
	How does money grow?
	



	
	Where should my money go first?
	



	
	How do I prepare my family for the future?
	



	
	How do I prepare myself for retirement?
	


Whether you attend one workshop or the entire series, you'll leave with practical knowledge and actionable steps to help you make informed financial decisions.

These workshops are for educational purposes only and are intended to provide general financial education. They should not be considered individualized financial, legal, tax, or investment advice.

title: Home Repair Essentials
location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, instructor Rob Haas will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

There is no assigned book—everyone is welcome to share what they're reading, discover new titles, and connect with others in the community while creating something by hand.

Bring a project you're working on, or start something new! Thanks to generous donations from our community, we'll often have a small selection of craft supplies available to share, though materials will vary from meeting to meeting.
