description:
Rich with emotional and social relevance, Mosaic Dance Theater Company’s world premiere production of Cassandra: An Ongoing Tragedy by award-winning playwright Ruth Cantrell, contrasts Greek myths to horrors of modern day, depicting the eternal existence of hate, and exploring the impact of the evils brought forth from Pandora's Box. The stories told in this piece, related by fictional characters in historical situations, are presented by a cast of 11, through live spoken word and dance, with a commissioned score of original music.

Directed by Morgiana Celeste Varricchio, with choreography by Samara Adell, and music by Michael V. Ficocelli.

This program is made possible by funds from the Essex County Division of Cultural and Historic Affairs, a partner of the New Jersey State Council on the Arts, and funding from The Puffin Foundation.

title: Zoom: Successfully Navigating College Admissions
description:
Register HERE





We are offering this Zoom presentation to help families of high school juniors, sophomores, and freshmen better understand the college admissions process and how to successfully navigate today’s changing landscape.

 

The session will cover current college admissions trends and strategies, the evolving test optional environment, the importance of researching and visiting colleges to find the right fit, and key timelines and action steps that can make this fall productive while easing stress around the college admissions process.

 

We will also take a close look at the holistic admissions review process, including what admissions officers value when evaluating applicants and how students can develop a strong personal narrative that reflects their strengths, interests, character, and experiences.

 

Another focus will be on the role of community service and the growing importance of meaningful “passion projects.” We will discuss how students can turn their interests, values, and experiences into authentic activities that foster personal growth, demonstrate character, and show positive impact. Admissions officers place great emphasis on character, and thoughtful service can help students show initiative, empathy, and a genuine commitment to helping their communities.

 

This program is recommended for parents and their high school teens. It provides a clear and strategic overview of what students should prioritize this fall for a successful college admissions journey and how to approach the process with confidence and less stress.

 

The presentation will be led by Ron Feuchs and Jackie Tepper, partners at Stand Out For College, LLC (www.standoutforcollege.com).

title: Book Talk: From the Abuelas' Window by Nancy Burke
location: Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
Join us for a book talk with author Nancy Burke about her book From the Abuelas' Window. The novel is currently being adapted for the musical stage!

About the book
It is Chile, 1974. Pinochet has taken over the presidential palace and the government far away in Santiago. The village school in a remote farming community has been closed and converted into a detention center for political prisoners. Maribel, a young girl in the village, is protected by her mother from the truth about her father who is among the prisoners but has been moved to an unknown place.

Three nosy old neighbors, the abuelas, love to peek out their window and watch Maribel and her sisters play innocent games in their mother's beautiful garden. They are rumored to have strange, magical powers, but stubborn and restless Maribel doesn't believe the rumors. She just wants her Papa, who she believes is visiting sick relatives, back so her mother doesn't depend on the abuelas for help.

A gift from the abuelas sets the story in motion and in a curiosity-driven moment, Maribel learns the truth about her father. The gift, an old red bicycle, takes her beyond the confines of her mother's garden and into the reality her mother can no longer keep from her.

Maribel responds by helping her mother bring food to the prisoners in her old school. She keeps a list of names of the innocent, hoping somewhere, someone is doing the same for her father.

The military comes in force to their village. Others are arrested, including Maribel's mother. The sisters discover a young girl, Sandra, hiding in their orchard. Her parents have been taken. Books are burned, songs are banned, but the village festival is held as usual, although under the watchful eye of the captain of the guard.

Maribel and her sisters take the power of love and magic, learned from the crafty old abuelas, into their own hands to change the course of fate for their family, their friends and a group of innocent strangers. Someone, somewhere, does the same for Papa.

About the Author
Nancy Burke is the author of Only the Women are Burning (2020), If I Could Paint the Moon Black (2014), From the Abuelas’ Window (2005) and a new short story collection, Death Cleaning and Other Units of Measure (2024). She holds an MFA in Fiction (Dramatic Writing concentration) from Rutgers’ University, Newark and a BA in Anthropology from Montclair State University. Her short stories have appeared in Pilgrim: A Journal of Catholic Experience, Meat for Tea: The Valley Review. At the Pool was a finalist for the J.F. Powers Award for Short Fiction at Dappled Things Literary Journal. Her screenplay adaptation of Only the Women are Burning won a Finalist recognition from the 2023 Boston Screenplay Competition. She is at work on a musical adaptation of From the Abuelas’ Window. Visit her Work in Progress page for info on this project. She teaches writing at New Jersey Institute of Technology and lives in Little Falls, NJ.

www.nancyburkestories.com

title: Ghosts, Grief, and Growing Up: YA Storytelling with Cherie Dimaline
description:
Step into the atmospheric and deeply moving world of storytelling with acclaimed Métis author Cherie Dimaline as we discuss her captivating body of work and her haunting Young Adult novel, Funeral Songs for Dying Girls.

Set in a cemetery shed where sixteen-year-old Winifred lives with her dad, Funeral Songs for Dying Girls follows a teen whose attempt to save her father's job leads to a fake ghost rumor—and accidentally summons a very real, opinionated spirit named Phil. Through this eerie yet heartwarming story, Dimaline crafts a haunting masterpiece about grief, survival, identity, and unexpected connections across the boundary of life and death. 

Beyond her graveyard-set YA novel, we will explore Dimaline’s expansive literary career—from the groundbreaking dystopian survival narrative of The Marrow Thieves and its sequel Hunting by Stars, to the dark, magic-infused folklore of her adult novels like Empire of Wild and VenCo.

Register today to participate in this spellbinding conversation!

 

About the Author: 

Cherie Dimaline is an internationally bestselling author. Her book The Marrow Thieves was named by TIME magazine, one of the Best YA Books of All Time and won the Governor General’s Award and the Kirkus Prize. Her novel Empire of Wild was an instant Canadian bestseller and is being adapted into a full opera for the Canadian Opera Company. Hunting By Stars was a 2022 American Indian Library Association Honor Book and her novel VENCO debuted at #1 on Canadian bestseller lists. Other titles include Funeral Songs for Dying Girls (AILA Honor Book, AURA Award winner, CRIME WRITERS Best Book, Bram Stoker Finalist) and Into the Bright Open (2024 Governor General’s Award Finalist).

Cherie lives in her Georgian Bay Métis Community and has written and produced for MARVEL, FX, HBO, Disney, and is currently adapting two major projects for AMC.

Get clear about what you want. Make bold decisions about what comes next. Leave with a practical plan to reclaim your life. 
You’ve spent years showing up for your career, your family, your relationships, and the people who depend on you. 
You’re capable. You’re responsible. You get things done.

title: Writing the Body - A Writing Workshop for Women
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Writing the Body – A Writing Workshop for Women
What can poetry say about our bodies that ordinary language can’t? How can our bodily experiences open new paths for our writing? 
In this generative workshop for women and nonbinary writers, Barbara O’Dair – poet, writer, and cofounder of the Park St. Writers Series – leads the group through readings, discussion, and writing exercises, using prompts to reveal fresh language, unexpected stories, and adventurous forms, and drawing from subjects such as body image, sexuality, desire, gender, illness, health, and aging. 
After a short grounding exercise, we’ll read and discuss a few poems that use the body and bodily experience to create meaning and music. Then we’ll write short pieces from three or four prompts. Everyone is encouraged to read their work aloud, and if time allows, the poet can take a few questions about their piece from the group. 
After a five-minute break, the second half of the workshop is devoted to writing a poem or creative piece and reading it aloud — either within the group, or as a “test drive” for the open mic later that evening. 
A few of the prompts (we may not get to all of them): 

If Your Body Could Talk… What would it say? Write a monologue in which one part of your body finally gets a chance to speak.
The Inherited Body. Finish this sentence: “I inherited my [body/hair/teeth] from…” Your parent is a natural choice, but consider more surprising options too — neighborhood, gender, class.
Medical Chart. Write a list of notes about your body that might appear on a medical chart, from a doctor’s POV. Then write your version: what should we know about you and your body? What does your version tell us about you?
Your Body in Time. Meet your body at eight, 25, 48, and today (or, if you’re under 40, work out the right ages). Introduce your different bodies to each other. Maybe your 48-year-old body wants a word with your eight-year-old body. About what?

Writing the Body – A Writing Workshop for Women 
Saturday, October 24, 4:30 – 6:30, $44 – price includes admission to the open mic.   
Workshop participants will be invited to read their work at the Space for Words open mic for writers that will follow the workshop later the same evening at 8pm.  The first portion of the open mic will be for workshop participants, and the second half is open to all women and female identifying persons. 
Learn more about the open mic here. 
 
Barbara O’Dair is a poet, writer, and cofounder of the Park St. Writers Series based in Montclair, NJ.

title: The Space for Words Open Mic — Women's Edition
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
The Space for Words Open Mic — Women’s Edition
Doors 7:30 · Start 8 PM · $10 for everyone 
Our monthly open mic returns for a special edition dedicated to women and female-identifying writers. 
The first portion of the night belongs to the workshop that is held before the open mic. Barbara O’Dair will lead a writing workshop that presents the theme ‘if your body could talk’.  Learn more about the workshop here.  Participants come up to read what they wrote that afternoon – new work, still warm, out loud for the first time. If you spent the evening writing about your body, this is where it gets to be heard. 
The second portion is open to all women and female-identifying persons. Bring your poetry, short stories, or excerpts from your latest work – the stage is yours. The Space is a safe place to try out new material, read old favorites, experiment with a different genre, and even to sing a song if inspiration strikes you. Put your name in the basket on your way in and you’ll get a shot at the mic, with a maximum of 5 minutes. Depending on how many people sign up and if time allows, we can have people come up a second time. 
Come for the words, stay for the community. The Space for Words has grown into an amazing community of writers supporting one another, and this night is about turning that room over to women’s voices for an evening. All levels, all genres — fiction, non-fiction, memoir, poetry. Afterward we take time to socialize and vibe with one another. 
You don’t have to do both. Come for the workshop, come for the open mic, or make a night of it. 

Good to know
Audience members are, as always, a welcome and vital part of these performances. 
If you have published books you’d like to sell, bring some copies and be prepared to accept payment. 
General guidelines: 

Hate speech of any kind is never allowed and will be shut down.
Violence or references to physical harm to others will be shut down.

BYOB is welcome, and some light snacks and drinks are served. 
Accessibility: The Space is located on the second floor of a historic building, accessible via a flight of stairs. Unfortunately, there is no elevator access at this time. This means we are unable to accommodate wheelchairs or guests with significant mobility challenges. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.

title: Susquehanna Super Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
It's been a long time since we've done a more difficult hike like this, but it's been a long time coming.
Since the son is going to "Trunk or Treat" with his mom, it is an opportunity to complete the final difficult section of the Conestoga Trail, as well as the next bit of the Mason-Dixon Trail in our rebooted series that we'd put on hold.
This promises to be challenging, but also very rewarding with views, history, and more.
After meeting at Pequea boat launch, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to our start point north of the Norman Wood Bridge.
We'll follow the Mason-Dixon Trail up to an overlook, and then down through a scenic gorge with small waterfalls. We then get on the towpath of the old Susquehanna and Tidewater Canal to Lock 12. This is the southern terminus of the Conestoga Trail.
We'll follow the Conestoga Trail across Norman Wood Bridge, and then up though lands to the north. Undulating terrain and beautiful vistas are throughout the section.
Pinnacle Rock and House Rock are among the best views on the entire trail. We'll also pass through lovely Tucquan Glen, and pass the Wind Cave, largest tectonic cave east of the Mississippi.
Those wanting more terrain and a bit more of a challenge than the other more recent hikes are going to love this one.
There are no food stops along the way. In fact, other than Norman Wood Bridge and two access roads, we won't even be crossing any roads on this one.
Distance will be normal, just over 15 miles. If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: Marking Movement: A Journey Through 5Rhythms and Intuitive Painting
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Marking Movement: A Journey Through 5Rhythms and Intuitive Painting
Sayrah Garrison and Naz Botas | October 25 | 1 – 3:30 pm | The Space | $55 — 12 spots available 
The Space invites you to give expression to your movements through intuitive painting.  This is not creation from the level of thought, but rather from your inner intuition and guidance. 
Marking Movement brings together two powerful languages of self-expression – 5Rhythms movement meditation and intuitive painting – into one continuous, embodied experience. 
The 5Rhythms Practice
Created by Gabrielle Roth, 5Rhythms is a conscious dance practice rooted in the principle that when we put the psyche in motion, it can begin to heal itself. The five rhythms – Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness – each offer a different quality of movement and energy, helping us cultivate grounded bodies, clear minds, and inspired spirits. 
Guided by the 5Rhythms map, we’ll take a deep dive into our own inner landscape, moving beyond choreography and expectations to reconnect with our authentic selves. As we become more present in our bodies, we create space to listen more deeply to what is moving through us, including the art that wants to emerge. 
From Movement to Mark-Making
We’ll move through the session in cycles: approximately ten minutes of dance followed by ten minutes of painting, repeating as we travel through the five rhythms. Rather than stopping to think about what to paint, you’ll carry the energy and sensation of each rhythm directly from the dance floor to the wall, allowing your hands to express what your body has just discovered. 
And there’s a twist: none of the paintings belong to just one person. 
All twelve stations – each one ready with its own large sheet of paper taped to the wall, along with colored chalk pastels, charcoal, tempera paint, brushes, and pencils – are shared by the whole group. Throughout the class, everyone moves from station to station, adding their mark to artwork others have already begun. 
By the end, twelve collaborative paintings will emerge, each one holding traces of the collective movement, energy, intuition, and presence of the entire group. There is no need to finish “your” piece and no ownership to protect. Instead, the paintings become a visual conversation, like the way we dance with one another.  One person’s Chaos layered over another’s Flowing, one moment of Stillness resting beside someone else’s Lyrical expression – it will all result in works of beauty. 
This is an opportunity to bring our deepest prayers to life through conscious movement and intuitive art, while experiencing the creative energy that emerges when we move and make in community. 
No dance experience or art experience is required.  Just bring a willingness to move without choreography and paint without a plan. Come ready to get out of your head, into your body, and onto the wall. 
What to Expect
Five rounds of 5Rhythms-inspired movement, each followed by ten minutes of free, intuitive painting at a shared station. All art supplies are provided. 
Wear comfortable clothing that allows you to move freely and that you don’t mind getting a little paint on. 
Space is limited to 12 participants to keep the experience intimate and the twelve shared paintings feeling personal and alive. 
Meet Your Facilitator
Sayrah Garrison is an accredited 5Rhythms teacher who lives and works in Northern New Jersey. She has been dancing the 5Rhythms since 2001 and teaching since 2014. A social worker and mother, Sayrah is passionate about the healing arts and the transformative potential of movement, creativity, and community. 
Join us for this unique wellness experience — a space to move, listen, create, and discover what wants to flow through you.

title: Classic Films Now: All the President’s Men
description:
Run Time: 140 minutes. Recommended for ages 13+. 
A nation distrusts its institutions. News has become spectacle. Ordinary people fight to matter. Welcome to 1976. 
Academy Award winners Robert Redford and Dustin Hoffman star in this true story as Washington Post reporters Carl Bernstein and Bob Woodward, whose investigation of a seemingly minor hotel room break-in uncovers the greatest political scandal in United States history and leads to the downfall of President Richard Nixon. 
 
Classic Films Now brings major works of cinema back to the big screen, films that not only defined their own time but continue to speak to ours. Each installment of the series gathers a group of landmark films curated around a theme, period, artist, or movement, inviting audiences to discover how the works connect with contemporary life. 
This fall, Classic Films Now kicks off with a three-film series devoted to 1976, a remarkable year in American cinema and a revealing moment in the nation’s cultural imagination. Released in the shadow of Watergate, Vietnam, urban crisis, and the Bicentennial, All the President’s Men, Network, and Rocky offer three sharply different portraits of American life at a time of great transition and uncertainty. 
Screenings will be introduced and hosted by Rafer Guzmán. Rafer writes about movies, music, and popular culture for Newsday. He has been a film critic for WNYC, a co-host of the independent podcast “Movie Therapy,” and a staff writer at The Wall Street Journal.

HOW IT WORKS: Bring your own book. Grab a seat.  Enjoy a quiet reading hour.

title: "All Over the World": The Geography of Rock, Jazz and More
location: Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Over two sessions, music historian Paul Groom will chronicle the stories from key locations in popular music history and highlight the links between them, how musicians adapted to new and creative developments which then become new industry standards. The presentations combine music, maps, musicians, narratives and memories!

Paul will highlight his travels to Memphis, Tenn.: Hamburg, Germany; Hawthorne, Calif.; Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; Central Avenue in Los Angeles; Abbey Road in London; La Caverne de la Huchette in Paris; Clarksdale, Miss.; West 70th Street in New York; S. Michigan Avenue in Chicago, Il; W. Rampart Street in New Orleans; Tupelo, Miss, Grand Boulevard in Detroit; Cleveland; Liverpool, England; the 9th Ward of New Orleans, 9137 S. title: Mental Health Support Group (NAMI's Connection Recovery Peer Support Group)
description:
The Essex-Passaic Chapter of NAMI (The National Alliance on Mental Illness) Connection Recovery Peer Support Group Program meets on the 4th Tuesday of each month at the West Caldwell Library on 30 Clinton Road. 

NAMI is the most influential organization devoted to helping people with mental illness and their relatives and loved ones recover and deal with mental health issues. These meetings will be led by people having some form of mental illness. During these meetings, we will conduct peer support though all people interested in this organization are encouraged to attend. You do not have to sign up in advance. All meetings are kept confidential and are led by people specifically trained to conduct these meetings.

 NAMI Connection is a recovery peer support group program that offers respect, understanding, encouragement and hope. NAMI Connection groups are:

·       Free and confidential

·       Held monthly for 90 minutes  

·       Designed to connect, encourage, and support participants using a structured support group model

·       Led by trained facilitators living in recovery themselves

This meeting is for anyone ages 18  who is dealing with their own mental illness or a loved one's.

This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

All eyes are on the midterm elections, and maps--both old and new--not only show how people vote but often help set and reinforce the patterns of how citizens are divided. First we'll take a look at maps of gerrymandering, which started in Massachusetts in 1811 and have taken very specific forms in the United States because of the rules of the American political system. We'll move onto the familiar red and blue election maps and examine how they privilege big, sparsely populated states like Wyoming over dense locations like New Jersey. We'll also take quick looks at great historical images, like Civil War-era election maps whose sectional splits look shockingly modern.

description:

description:

To Participate: RSVP to attend the event each week. Meet in Blanton Hall Residence Hall Kitchenette in the Communal Area (Tell them you are working with Food Recovery), Sign in via Event Pass and your set!
Requirements:

Volunteers must be Food Safe Certified to participate.
Complete the certification by following the step-by-step instructions provided in this link.
Once certified, email your certification to foodrecoverynetwork@sgamsu.org to confirm your eligibility to participate.

Your involvement helps reduce food waste and insecurity while supporting individuals in our community who are in need. We look forward to your participation!*Please Note: This event end time is dependent on the amount of food given. You can estimate for max of hour and a half for recoveries.

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Craft Supply Swap Donation Days!
description:
We are collecting your new/like-new/gently-used craft supplies and finding them a new home where they will be used! 

Donation Days:  


	
	Donate items from Saturday October 31 through Friday November 6 only, during regular library hours.
	
	
	Please limit to 1-2 bags or boxes.
	
	
	Bring to the Reference Desk.
	
	
	If you donate supplies, you will receive a ticket for admission to the first hour of the swap.
	


Guidelines:


	Items should be new or very gently used, clean and dry, free from damage and mildew, in good working condition.
	Small items (e.g. beads) or sets of items (e.g. markers) should be bagged together.
	All items should be easily lifted and carried by one person.
	The library has the right to refuse or recycle items.


Suggested Items -- including but not limited to:


	
	beads and jewelry making supplies
	
	
	brushes, canvases, unopened paint
	
	
	knitting needles, crochet hooks, yarn
	
	
	unopened clay
	
	
	ribbon, fabric, trim, embroidery thread, needles
	
	
	scrapbook paper, stickers, scissors and punches
	
	
	drawing supplies (pencils, markers)
	
	
	small sewing or craft machines
	
	
	craft kits or supplies for kids

title: SMC Trail Work Volunteer Day
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**TRAIL WORK will continue rerouting the Hogenauer Trail** (we are making progress!) up the slope and away from recently installed property fences. **Meet At:** Dog Park/ Wildflower Preserve, 11 Bear Lane, Maplewood. From there, we will walk to Crater View on Crest drive and then to the Hogenauer trail work site. (Note: While we normally meet the first Sudnay of each month, this volunteer day was shifted after the Labor Day weekend.)

Trail work is physically challenging but very satisfying as we use hand tools to build and repair trails. Participants must be 15+ years. Those younger than 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Participants **should wear long pants** due to [ticks](https://www.somocon.org/?page_id=193928&fb) and thron bushes and sturdy shoes, and bring gloves (though backup gloves will be available). Tools, water, and a snack will be provided. (Registration is not required though if you sign up on Meetup, it helps us know how many tools to bring.) Only heavy, steady rain cancels.

title: Classic Films Now: Network
description:
Run Time: 121 Minutes. Recommended for ages 18+ 
A nation distrusts its institutions. News has become spectacle. Ordinary people fight to matter. Welcome to 1976. 
Best Picture nominee about a mentally unstable news anchor who, after being told he’s to be fired, becomes a media superstar when he begins delivering nightly rants and threatens an on-air suicide for his final broadcast. Paddy Chayevsky’s script won an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay; Peter Firth received a posthumous Best Actor award as the unhinged newsman; and Faye Dunaway won Best Actress as a scheming network exec. 
 
Classic Films Now brings major works of cinema back to the big screen, films that not only defined their own time but continue to speak to ours. Each installment of the series gathers a group of landmark films curated around a theme, period, artist, or movement, inviting audiences to discover how the works connect with contemporary life. 
This fall, Classic Films Now kicks off with a three-film series devoted to 1976, a remarkable year in American cinema and a revealing moment in the nation’s cultural imagination. Released in the shadow of Watergate, Vietnam, urban crisis, and the Bicentennial, All the President’s Men, Network, and Rocky offer three sharply different portraits of American life at a time of great transition and uncertainty. 
Screenings will be introduced and hosted by Rafer Guzmán. Rafer writes about movies, music, and popular culture for Newsday. He has been a film critic for WNYC, a co-host of the independent podcast “Movie Therapy,” and a staff writer at The Wall Street Journal.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - Reclaiming Your Inner Wisdom: Sacred Indigenous Teachings with Asha Frost
description:
You must register here to attend:  https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/217344



In a fast-paced world that often leaves us feeling overwhelmed and disconnected, true healing does not come from looking outward—it begins within. Join us for a transformative virtual conversation with Indigenous Medicine Woman Asha Frost as she explores her groundbreaking book, You Are the Medicine: 13 Indigenous Teachings to Connect to Your Inner Wisdom, Reclaim Your Power, and Heal.

The Medicine you have been searching for lives within you. Follow the path of the 13 Ojibwe Moons with Animal Spirits and Ancestors as your guides as you unlock your connection to your own unique, inherent healing power. Through storytelling, ceremonies, and Shamanic journeys, learn to apply ancient wisdom to your life in ways that are respectful and conscious of the stolen lands, lives, and traditions of Indigenous peoples.

Discover how to:

- Ground and root into your own lineage and meet your Ancestral guides.
- Practice self-care and rest on your journey.
- Return to Ancestral ways of cleansing and purifying.
- Trust and surrender so you can manifest and thrive.
- Release self-doubt, fear, disconnection, and insecurity.

Register now and take the first step toward recognizing and reclaiming your innate wisdom. 

About the Author: 

Asha Frost (she/her) is an Indigenous Medicine Woman and a member of the Chippewas of Nawash First Nation. She is from the Crane Clan, the totem of leadership, and believes in holding space from vision and heart. As an energy healer, homeopath, and mentor, Asha has guided thousands of people through profound and lasting transformation.

Impacted by generational trauma and colonization, Asha has been on a lifelong journey of reclamation. A lupus diagnosis sent her on a path of studying and practicing a multitude of energy Medicine modalities with many guides. She has blended this life experience with her innate gifts and the wisdom of her Ancestors. She loves sharing her Medicine in powerful ways through Ceremonies, teachings, and speaking events. Through this work, she loves seeing people reclaim their roots, find their healing wisdom, and rise into their power.

Asha lives on Anishinaabe, Huron-Wendat, and Haudenosaunee Territory, with her husband and two beautiful children, with whom she co-creates a better world for the seven generations to come.

title: The American Experiment: Information, Power, and Democracy: The First Amendment
description:
Join President Koppell for his first lecture in the American Experiment series, where he will discuss Information, Power, and Democracy: The First Amendment.
The First Amendment is the cornerstone of American democracy because it guarantees the fundamental freedoms required for citizens to govern themselves, including freedom of speech, freedom of the press, and freedom of assembly.  Citizens need access to open debate, diverse viewpoints, and accurate information in order to make informed decisions. These freedoms also protect unpopular and minority opinions and act as a check on the state from censoring speech or controlling what people learn, think, and say.  This lecture examines the foundational freedoms of the First Amendment and how they are applied to contemporary American democratic life, including: the impact of money on expression, the role of new media and corporate media, the role of the press in investigating and disseminating information, the right to protest as a form of assembly and expression, and the challenges posed by misinformation, disinformation, polarization, fragmented media audiences, and declining public trust. At its center is a fundamental question for American democracy: What are the inherent rights and responsibilities of freedom of expression in a democratic society?





Hosted by: Campus Activities, Civic & Voter Engagement

description:
Join us for an exciting Midterm Election Night Party on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, from 7 to 10 p.m. in the Fish Bowl, located in the School of Communication and Media lobby!
Come together with members of the campus community to watch the midterm election results unfold in real time. Follow the action and see who will prevail in New Jersey’s 12 U.S. House of Representatives districts, while also keeping an eye on other key races from across the country.
Hosted by the Office of Civic and Voter Engagement, the Department of Political Science and Law, the Political Science Club, and the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, the event will offer a lively and welcoming space to discuss the races, exchange insights, and experience democracy in action.

title: Working with Your Angels, Guides & Master Teachers by RoseMarie Rubinetti Cappiello
description:
Join the West Caldwell Public Library in welcoming Bergen County NJ Author RoseMarie Rubinetti Cappiello;  Intuitive/Medium/Healer, Hospice Trained Grief Volunteer, Ordained Spiritual Minister, Certified Hypnotherapist, Yoga Instructor, Reiki Attuned, BS Physical Education MSU and Author of Speaking From Spirit. 

EVENT WILL TAKE PLACE AT THE TOWN HALL (30 CLINTON RD, 2ND FLOOR)

Do you feel connected to Spirit, higher intelligence– a consciousness greater than you? Do you actively call on this source for support to help you in your day to day life? What if you could access this creative force in a tangible, practical and authoritative way? We will discuss this often under-utilized resource and how to work with it in a more conscious and powerful way. We will call on and build our connection to our unseen helpers—who are always helping us anyway whether we believe in them or not- and build our success teams for health and wellness and for financial support, guidance, success, assistance and structure. We will call on the relationship specialists and even the ones for career guidance and direction. Just as there are people with special gifts and skills on Earth that can assist us- Higher Consciousness/Heaven is filled with such guides, teachers, helpers and angels that have specialties too. Come meet the teams, build the teams and work with the behind the scenes helpers that work with you. When you work consciously with your spirit teams you will notice that life just seems to work out easier. Things start falling into place miraculously. Details get ironed out and things come together in a perfect way. You will always be in the right place at the right time, meeting the right people and opportunities and resources show up in unexpected ways. This class can be taken over and over again to gain even more insight, help and support from spirit. This is truly life changing information. Please bring a notebook and pen.

Trained by the best teachers from Arthur Findlay College in England, RoseMarie has highly developed psychic, mediumistic, intuitive, healing abilities. She has worked professionally as a Medium/Intuitive/Healer since 2000 and has connected many people to their loved ones in Spirit through thousands of private medium readings and platform medium demonstrations throughout the United States. Many people claim their lives change dramatically after having a reading with her and that the weight of grief and sadness significantly decreases.

In addition, she is a Spiritual Teacher who teaches online classes in psychic-spiritual development and conducts live classes in many venues across the country. Some topics covered are Telepathy, Dream Interpretation, Psychic Studies, Mediumship Development and Understanding the Soul and Spirit.

She is also a regressionist who does private and group healing work and Other Life Regression (often referred to as Past Life Regression).

Through her hospice training she often works with people and their families as they are getting ready to transition. She feels completely privileged and blessed to do this work.

Lastly, she is an adjunct professor at Montclair State University NJ where she teaches yoga in the physical education department.

title: Secrets, Lies, and Unforgettable Twists: A Conversation with E. Lockhart
description:
Join us for an exciting author talk with #1 New York Times bestselling author E. Lockhart as we reflect on her impressive body of work, including the literary sensation We Were Liars, and even gain an exclusive sneak peek into her shimmering new thriller, The Pools. 

Once, in a small New England town known for its hot springs, something terrible happened. Something that should have been a warning to stay away from the pools, if the stories were to be believed.

But no one is afraid of the water anymore, even if they should be.

When new girl Lexie meets golden boy Chester, their chemistry is undeniable. She’s running from a glittering life she won’t speak about. He’s hiding secrets of his own. Their connection feels bigger than both of them, despite their damage.

One frigid winter morning in that small New England town, five people go for a swim in the pools. Five people, including Chester. What happens there sends shock waves through the town, changing life as Lexie knows it forever.

Register now to step into the gripping, suspenseful worlds of E. Lockhart and ask questions live!

 

About the Author: 

Lockhart is the #1 New York Times bestselling author of the LIARS novels: We Were Liars, Family of Liars, and We Fell Apart. We Were Liars is also an original series on Prime Video. Her other books include Again Again, Genuine Fraud, and The Disreputable History of Frankie Landau-Banks. She has been a finalist for the Los Angeles Times Book Prize and the National Book Award and an honoree for the Printz Award. She lives in Brooklyn, New York.

title: 1st International Symposium of Latino Oral History
description:
Join us for the First International Symposium of Latino Oral History, “Listening as Resistance: Oral History, Memory and the Latino Experience” taking place virtually on November 6–7. This two-day symposium will bring together scholars, students, educators, writers, and community members to explore the power of oral history and Latino storytelling as tools for preserving lived experiences, amplifying voices, and challenging dominant historical narratives.
We are honored to welcome acclaimed writer, journalist, and University of California, Irvine professor Héctor Tobar as our keynote speaker.
We invite participants to submit an abstract to present their work or register to attend and learn more about Latino storytelling and oral history practices.
Best paper will get a chance to be published in an academic journal.
Student registration is free.
Please register for the symposium with the link below:
https://montclair.co1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cYowQOHwct2em0K
To submit an abstract: 
 https://montclair.co1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_1N6j22Uqp6ulqiq

Hosted by: Association of Latino Professionals For America, Bloomfield Student Life, Bloomfield Lambda Sigma Upsilon Latino Fraternity, Inc., Center for Latino Heritage & Spanish Language Excellence, Dominican Student Organization, Ecuadorian Students Association, Latin American Student Organization, Latin@ Caucus, Mexican-American Student Association, Office for Hispanic Initiatives, Puerto Rican Student Organization, Peruvian-American Student Organization, Student Life At Montclair (SLAM), Spanish and Latino Studies

title: Craft Supply Swap
location: Nutley - Stockton Room, Nutley Free Public Library
description:
We are collecting your new/like-new/gently-used craft supplies and finding them a new home where they will be used! 

Donation Days:  


	
	Donate items from Saturday October 31 through Friday November 6 only, during regular library hours.
	
	
	Please limit to 1-2 bags or boxes.
	
	
	Bring to the Reference Desk.
	
	
	If you donate supplies, you will receive a ticket for admission to the first hour of the swap.
	


The Day of the Swap - Rules and Timeline:


	
	Saturday, November 7: Please do not bring any new donations!
	
	
	On arrival, swappers will each receive one shopping bag to fill.
	
	
	1:30 - 2:30 -- the first hour is limited to those who donated materials (you must bring your ticket!)
	
	
	2:30 - 3:30 -- the second hour is open to everyone (limit one bag)
	
	
	3:30 - 4:00 -- unlimited supply pickup
	
	
	Any items remaining at the end will be donated to local organizations or kept for library programming.
	


Guidelines:


	Items should be new or very gently used, clean and dry, free from damage and mildew, in good working condition.
	Small items (e.g. beads) or sets of items (e.g. markers) should be bagged together.
	All items should be easily lifted and carried by one person.
	The library has the right to refuse or recycle items.


Suggested Items -- including but not limited to:


	
	beads and jewelry making supplies
	
	
	brushes, canvases, unopened paint
	
	
	knitting needles, crochet hooks, yarn
	
	
	unopened clay
	
	
	ribbon, fabric, trim, embroidery thread, needles
	
	
	scrapbook paper, stickers, scissors and punches
	
	
	drawing supplies (pencils, markers)
	
	
	small sewing or craft machines
	
	
	craft kits or supplies for kids
	


You do not need to be a Nutley cardholder or resident.  Please call 973-667-0405 ext. 2604, or email marisa.treglio@nutley.bccls.org with any questions!

title: PRE-ADVENT BEGINS
description: At Holy Spirit Verona we share in three weeks of "Pre-Advent" -- the three Sundays between All Saints and Advent 1. During this time we encourage you to take an intentional “pause” before the waiting and preparing of Advent. Advent used to be seven weeks, up until the 7th century, and there is a small movement within the Church to return to that (see theadventproject.org). Many of the scripture readings and prayers after All Saints give a hint or lean towards Advent, so Father Jerry says... why not just go there!Yes, we all know Father Jerry loves Advent. We are not bringing forth Christmas early like many retailers do, but rather allowing an intentional time to PAUSE before the all-consuming month of December. These three weeks of Pre-Advent, we hope, will bring forth a level of preparation and space during Advent which will make Christmas that much more meaningful. Our first experience of Pre-Advent was in 2018, so it's now officially a tradition! We get to see the blue hangings, which are symbolic of the Blessed Mother, for just a few extra weeks. Find some space these next three weeks to do something that will set you up well for the entrance of the Christ-child into our midst yet again. Join us as we prepare to prepare!
source: Church of the Holy Spirit Verona

title: Classic Films Now: Rocky
description:
Run Time: 120 minutes, recommended for ages 11+ 
A nation distrusts its institutions. News has become spectacle. Ordinary people fight to matter. Welcome to 1976. 
A club fighter from Philadelphia who moonlights as a collector for a local mobster gets a shot at the big time when the heavyweight champion of the world gives him chance to fight for the belt on America’s bicentennial. 
 
Classic Films Now brings major works of cinema back to the big screen, films that not only defined their own time but continue to speak to ours. Each installment of the series gathers a group of landmark films curated around a theme, period, artist, or movement, inviting audiences to discover how the works connect with contemporary life. 
This fall, Classic Films Now kicks off with a three-film series devoted to 1976, a remarkable year in American cinema and a revealing moment in the nation’s cultural imagination. Released in the shadow of Watergate, Vietnam, urban crisis, and the Bicentennial, All the President’s Men, Network, and Rocky offer three sharply different portraits of American life at a time of great transition and uncertainty. 
Screenings will be introduced and hosted by Rafer Guzmán. Rafer writes about movies, music, and popular culture for Newsday. He has been a film critic for WNYC, a co-host of the independent podcast “Movie Therapy,” and a staff writer at The Wall Street Journal.

description:
**The Future is Peace: An Evening with Peace Activits Maoz Inon & Aziz Abu Sarah**  
Please join NIF in partnership with Temple Ner Tamid, B'nai Keshet, and Congregation Shomrei Emunah.  
  
Talk, with Reception to follow  
  
**Aziz Abu Sarah** is a Palestinian peacemaker, co-founder of InterAct International, and co-author with Maoz Inon of The Future Is Peace. The loss of his brother, who had been detained in an Israeli prison, was a turning point. Aziz's grief and initial desire for revenge transformed into a lifelong commitment to reconciliation. From his roots in Jerusalem, he has become a global advocate for peace, implementing projects in over 80 countries. In 2009 he co-founded MEJDI Tours, introducing the groundbreaking Dual Narrative™ approach with Israeli and Palestinian guides leading tours together.  
  
**Maoz Inon** is an Israeli social entrepreneur, co-founder of InterAct International, and co-author with Aziz Abu Sarah of The Future Is Peace. After losing his parents in the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023, Maoz transformed his grief into a global call for reconciliation. From grassroots communities to universities, parliaments, and international forums, he inspires audiences with his conviction that “Peace is possible” and “Hope is an action.”  
  
**ABOUT NIF:** The New Israel Fund is the leading organization advancing and defending democracy in Israel. Widely credited with building Israeli progressive civil society, we have provided over $345 million to more than 950 organizations since our inception in 1979. title: How Money Became God: Rethinking Wealth and Greed in Modern Society with Paul Vigna
description:
Join us for an eye-opening conversation with veteran journalist Paul Vigna as we examine his provocative book, The Almightier: How Money Became God, Greed Became Virtue, and Debt Became Sin, in which he explores the question: how did money go from a tool of commerce into the dominant faith of modern society? 

In The Almightier, Vigna takes readers on a sweeping historical journey from Renaissance Florence to today’s global financial markets, revealing how wealth accumulation evolved from a moral failing into an unspoken civic virtue. He uncovers the forgotten history of money, tracing the uneasy and often accidental alliance between wealth and religion as it developed from ancient city-states to today’s secular world, where religious devotion has receded and greed has stepped in to fill the void. 

Through engaging anecdotes, original research, and fresh perspectives on the causes of the many challenges we face today, Vigna makes a compelling argument that money has no power apart from the power we give it.

Whether you are interested in economic history, personal finance, or the hidden cultural forces shaping modern life, this talk is sure to pique your interest. 

Register today to learn more about how devotion to money has replaced religion as the foundation of our society.

 

About the Author: 

Paul Vigna is an author, journalist, editor and speaker, with a particular focus on capital markets and cryptocurrencies. He is the author of Guts: The Anatomy of The Walking Dead and coauthor of The Age of Cryptocurrency and The Truth Machine. For 25 years, he was a reporter and editor for Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal, pioneering coverage of the cryptocurrency sector. He has appeared on CNN, CNBC, MSNBC, Fox, and PBS.

title: Fire, Passion, and Heritage: Native American and Mexican Cooking with Chef Pyet DeSpain
description:
Prepare your palate for a vibrant culinary journey with star chef Pyet DeSpain, the inaugural winner of Gordon Ramsay’s hit television competition Next Level Chef, as she presents her debut cookbook, Rooted in Fire: A Celebration of Native American and Mexican Cooking. 

Pyet DeSpain rose to prominence as the first winner of Gordon Ramsey’s Fox television show Next Level Chef. Now, in her debut cookbook, she shares the joy of cooking fueled by her burning passion for Native American and Mexican American cuisine. 

Pyet shows you how to incorporate a delicious range of key ingredients—from venison, dandelion greens, to sunchokes, bison, and native berries—into more than sixty fusion dishes. Family and friends will be excited to gather around the table to enjoy sweet and savory food such as:


	Three Sisters Salad
	Bison and Sweet Corn Soup
	Fry Bread
	Mexican Chocolate & Mezcal Cake
	Corn Silk and Honey Tea
	Wojapi BBQ Sauce


Rooted in Fire is far more than just a collection of recipes; it is a movement giving voice to Indigenous culture, histories, and foodways through the universal language of food.

Register for this event today and learn how to work with nature in your own kitchen.

 

About the Author: 

Pyet—short for her inherited Native American name, Pyetwetmokwe—is a member of the Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation and an award-winning global private chef. She made history as the first winner of Gordon Ramsay’s Next Level Chef and was named one of Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top 25 Private Chefs in Los Angeles. Her work is centered on uplifting Indigenous foodways within the culinary industry while advocating for a more sustainable and sovereign food system for Indigenous peoples.

title: John Lennon – Life, Legend and Legacy.
description:
About the program 

The real beginning of The Beatles took place at a summer garden fete at St. Peter's Church in Woolton, Liverpool, on July 6, 1957, marking a watershed point in music history. When John Lennon was 16 years old and performing with his skiffle band The Quarrymen, a common acquaintance called Ivan Vaughan, introduced him to Paul McCartney, who was 15 years old at the time. This one-of-a-kind partnership altered the course of music irrevocably, and our presenter will trace its history.

About the Artist

John Paul Groom, originally from Liverpool, resided in the same city as John Lennon and George Harrison, participated in the same Sunday school as John Lennon, and went to the same high school as Paul McCartney and George Harrison. Numerous cherished recollections that I will be presenting in this discourse

title: NJ Code & Coffee - November meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

\*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,

* What you can help others with,
\*What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

title: Side By Side: Delving into Israeli and Palestinian Narratives, Part II
location: Congregation Shomrei Emunah, 67 Park St, Montclair, NJ 07042, USA, Social Hall
description:
**Side By Side: Delving into Israeli and Palestinian Narratives, Part II**  
A Learning Series led by Rabbi Justus Baird   
  
A three-part series exploring dual narratives of events in Israel/Palestine, specifically from Israeli Jewish and Palestinian points of view. The goal of the series is not to debate those narratives nor change our own, but simply to hear and engage with them.  
  
In this session, we will focus on narratives of the early Zionist movement and Jewish immigration, up to and including the Balfour Declaration and its impact (1880s - 1920).   
  
Advance reading, approximately two book chapters, is required. Please register so that Rabbi Justus can share pre-reading materials with you before the class.   
  
**Registration**: https://shomrei.easyshul.com/events/6ac90befe0b01c00261147e5  
  
Participants should expect the learning to be challenging and difficult, emotionally and psychologically.  
  
This session is open to all, whether you attended Part I of the series or not.   
  
The first session, on May 17, covered the establishment of the State of Israel, what Palestinians call the Naqba. The third and final session, scheduled for January 10, will explore the First Intifada.  
  
Please remember to bring your fob to access the building.

title: Zoom: Successfully Navigating College Admissions
description:
Register HERE





We are offering this Zoom presentation to help families of high school juniors, sophomores, and freshmen better understand the college admissions process and how to successfully navigate today’s changing landscape.

 

The session will cover current college admissions trends and strategies, the evolving test optional environment, the importance of researching and visiting colleges to find the right fit, and key timelines and action steps that can make this fall productive while easing stress around the college admissions process.

 

We will also take a close look at the holistic admissions review process, including what admissions officers value when evaluating applicants and how students can develop a strong personal narrative that reflects their strengths, interests, character, and experiences.

 

Another focus will be on the role of community service and the growing importance of meaningful “passion projects.” We will discuss how students can turn their interests, values, and experiences into authentic activities that foster personal growth, demonstrate character, and show positive impact. Admissions officers place great emphasis on character, and thoughtful service can help students show initiative, empathy, and a genuine commitment to helping their communities.

 

This program is recommended for parents and their high school teens. It provides a clear and strategic overview of what students should prioritize this fall for a successful college admissions journey and how to approach the process with confidence and less stress.

 

The presentation will be led by Ron Feuchs and Jackie Tepper, partners at Stand Out For College, LLC (www.standoutforcollege.com).

title: Epic Worlds and Celestial Prophecies: Exploring the Between Earth and Sky Trilogy with Rebecca Roanhorse
description:
Step into a sprawling world of celestial magic, political intrigue, and ancient prophecies with New York Times bestselling author Rebecca Roanhorse as we dive deep into her acclaimed Between Earth and Sky trilogy. Black Sun, Fevered Star, and Mirrored Heavens are inspired by the rich and diverse cultures of the pre-Columbian Americas, reshaping modern speculative fiction with unmissable worldbuilding.

Black Sun, the first book in the trilogy, introduces us to the holy city of Tova. The winter solstice is usually a time for celebration and renewal, but this year it coincides with a solar eclipse, a rare celestial event proscribed by the Sun Priest as an unbalancing of the world.

Meanwhile, a ship launches from a distant city bound for Tova and set to arrive on the solstice. The captain of the ship, Xiala, is a disgraced Teek whose song can calm the waters around her as easily as it can warp a man’s mind. Her ship carries one passenger. Described as harmless, the passenger, Serapio, is a young man, blind, scarred, and cloaked in destiny. As Xiala well knows, when a man is described as harmless, he usually ends up being a villain.

Whether you are a longtime fan of the trilogy or searching for your next immersive fantasy read, this is an event you won’t want to miss out on.

Register today to go behind the scenes with one of speculative fiction's most exciting voices!

 

About the Author: 

Rebecca Roanhorse is a New York Times bestselling and Nebula, Hugo, and Locus Award-winning speculative fiction writer. She has published multiple award-winning short stories and novels, including two novels in The Sixth World series, Star Wars: Resistance Reborn, Race to the Sun for the Rick Riordan imprint, and the Hugo Award-winning epic fantasy trilogy Between Earth and Sky. She was the guest editor of America’s Best Science Fiction and Fantasy (2023) and a contributor to the New York Times “100 Best Books of the 21st Century.” She has also written for Marvel comics and games, and her TV writing includes FX’s A Murder at the End of the World, and the Marvel series Echo for Disney . She has had her own work optioned by Paramount, Amazon Studios, Netflix, and AMC Studios.

title: Parish Hike and Potluck
description: Join us for abeautiful hike to Tripod Rock, located at the Pyramid Mountain Natural HistoricArea in Montville. We will meet at the church parking lot at 8:45am tocaravan or carpool to the trailhead. The hike should take about 2 1/2 hours.Wear sturdyshoes and bring water,snacks, and hiking poles (if you have them). Dogs are welcome on the trails butmust be kept on leash at all times. Potluck at Church after hike!MOREINFORMATION ABOUT THE PARISH HIKE:The 3-mile loophike begins with a 300 foot climb along the Blue Trail, where we will berewarded with an unobstructed view of the New York City skyline. (It's a prettysteep climb, but once we get to the top it's mostly flat.) We will continue onthe Blue trail to the Blue Dot trail which leads to a unique glacial erraticknown as Tripod Rock. This renowned, multi-ton boulder is balanced on threesmall boulders, and was deposited by the Wisconsin Glacier over 18,000 years ago.We will then backtrack to the Blue Trail, descend another steep climb and walkalongside the Taylortown Reservoir.  For over 10,000 years, this wildernessland provided shelter and served as a hunting, fishing, and gathering site forthe Lenape Indians, who may have used Tripod Rock as a celestialcalendar. Later, notorious outlaws used the region as a hide-out, while 19thcentury explorers and traders came and went.  At theconclusion of the hike (which is rated "Moderate") we can check outthe visitor’s center which features Indian artifacts and other exhibits. Joinfor potluck at the Church after that!Sign-up in theFellowship Hall or email Father Jerry at rector@holyspiritverona. Questions?See parishioner Ruth Portela.
source: Church of the Holy Spirit Verona

title: The Hands Free & Dance Heginbotham: The Party Scene
description:
Exquisitely eclectic quartet The Hands Free and members of the fabulously whimsical Dance Heginbotham join forces in The Party Scene. Inspired by The Nutcracker and your holiday office party, this music and dance extravaganza is part Drosselmeyer and part Turkey Lurkey Time. Lightly immersive and family friendly, The Party Scene features student party guests from Montclair State University. All guests are encouraged to don impressively festive seasonal sweaters. 
 
About The Hands Free: The Hands Free is an acoustic quartet, bringing together the creative voices of composer/performers James Moore (guitar & banjo), Caroline Shaw (violin), Nathan Koci (accordion), and Eleonore Oppenheim (bass). Drawing from an eclectic array of influences in classical, jazz and folk traditions, the group produces a unique and evocative blend of joyful melodies, lush sonic textures and explosive improvisations. 
About Dance Heginbotham: Dance Heginbotham (DH) is a New York-based contemporary dance company committed to supporting, producing, and performing the work of choreographer John Heginbotham. With an emphasis on collaboration, DH enriches national and international communities with its unique blend of inventive, thoughtful, and rigorous dance theater works. Founded in 2011, DH had its world premiere in January 2012 at The Kennedy Center and has been presented by major venues throughout the US including Bard SummerScape, Brooklyn Academy of Music, Hopkins Center for the Arts, Jacob’s Pillow Dance Festival, The Joyce Theater, Lincoln Center, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, and Works Process at The Guggenheim, among many others. DH has shared the stage with luminaries of the music world including Alarm Will Sound, Brooklyn Rider, The Knights, National Symphony Orchestra, Joshua Bell, André de Ridder, and Eric Jacobsen, and has commissioned new scores from composers Tyondai Braxton, Ethan Iverson, and Colin Jacobsen. DH has collaborated with designers and artists Maira Kalman, Isaac Mizrahi, Amy Trompetter, Maile Okamura, and Nicole Pearce in the creation of new works. 
www.danceheginbotham.org

title: Mental Health Support Group (NAMI's Connection Recovery Peer Support Group)
description:
The Essex-Passaic Chapter of NAMI (The National Alliance on Mental Illness) Connection Recovery Peer Support Group Program meets on the 4th Tuesday of each month at the West Caldwell Library on 30 Clinton Road. 

NAMI is the most influential organization devoted to helping people with mental illness and their relatives and loved ones recover and deal with mental health issues. These meetings will be led by people having some form of mental illness. During these meetings, we will conduct peer support though all people interested in this organization are encouraged to attend. You do not have to sign up in advance. All meetings are kept confidential and are led by people specifically trained to conduct these meetings.

 NAMI Connection is a recovery peer support group program that offers respect, understanding, encouragement and hope. NAMI Connection groups are:

·       Free and confidential

·       Held monthly for 90 minutes  

·       Designed to connect, encourage, and support participants using a structured support group model

·       Led by trained facilitators living in recovery themselves

This meeting is for anyone ages 18  who is dealing with their own mental illness or a loved one's.

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

More than a million members gather in person, online, and in destinations around the world to read together and swap stories. All readers are welcome!

HOW IT WORKS: Bring your own book. Grab a seat.  Enjoy a quiet reading hour. 

There are no assigned readings, no pressure to socialize. All book formats are welcome (headphones for audiobooks). 

From 5:30-6pm, participants arrive, find their seats and chat with other book lovers about what you are reading. 

From 6-7pm, please enjoy the quiet reading hour and from 7-7:30pm you can continue to read or socialize.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - Sparks, Shadows, and Epic Romantasy with Helen Scheuerer
description:
You must register here to attend:  https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/224402



Join us virtually for a downright intoxicating conversation with bestselling fantasy author Helen Scheuerer as we delve into her thrilling new novel, Kiss of the Black Flame.

Some bargains are sealed with blood. Others with fire. The deadliest are sealed with a kiss...

Saige Grayson has always believed stories could heal—even when her own body refuses to. As the most promising bookbinder in the capital, she’s learned to work through chronic pain and crushing debt, restoring other people’s treasures while trying not to fall apart herself. But when the man she owes decides her rare talent is worth more than her payments, Saige is traded to the Azkari—an immortal race forged by the gods for war—and imprisoned in their ancient stronghold.

Her only chance of survival lies with Archer, a fallen Azkari general imprisoned beside her—cursed, dangerous, and impossible to ignore. He offers her a way out, and in return, Saige must help him retrieve and restore an ancient book. But the book is made of living magic, powerful enough to stop a great evil—or unleash it. And as Saige works with Archer, the tome begins to awaken something dark and dangerous—both in the realm and within her.

As their enemies close in and buried memories resurface, Saige and Archer must decide what they’re willing to sacrifice: their freedom, their fragile trust…or the spark that could ignite the world.

Register now to take part in the magic–and the spice–of Helen’s newest book!

About the Author: 

Helen Scheuerer is a Sunday Times (London) bestselling author best known for her romantasy series, The Legends of Thezmarr and The Ashes of Thezmarr. Her work has been highly praised for its strong, flawed female characters and its action-packed plots. Helen’s love of writing and books led her to pursue a creative writing degree and a Master's of Publishing. She has been a full-time author since 2018 and is constantly dreaming up new stories.

title: The Space for Words - Literary Open mic with NJ Poetry Circle
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
The Space for Words – Literary Open mic hosted with the NJ Poetry Circle
December 4  |  Doors open at 7:30, start time 8 pm  |  $10 for everyone 
This is a monthly event on the last Friday of every month, holidays permitting. 
Hey writers, poets, and storytellers!  Come share your art with us at The Space for Words Open Mic Night. Whether you’re a seasoned author or just getting started, this is your chance to share your work in front of a supportive and inspiring audience. 
Bring your poetry, short stories, or excerpts from your latest work — the stage is yours! The Space is a safe place to try out new material, read old favorites, experiment with a different genre, and even to sing a song if inspiration strikes you. Each performer gets a maximum of 5 minutes to read, and at the end we take time to socialize and vibe with one another. 
Come for the words, stay for the community. The Space for Words has grown into an amazing community of writers supporting one another. This event is open to all levels and all genres, so whether you write fiction, non-fiction, memoir, or poetry, we want to hear from you. It’s all about celebrating the power of storytelling in a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere. All of our open mic nights are always inclusive. 
Anyone who puts their name in the bucket upon entry gets a shot at the mic, and has a maximum of 5 minutes. Depending on how many people sign up and if time allows, we can have people come up a second time. 
Audience members are, as always, a welcome and vital part of these performances. 
If you have published books that you would like to sell, bring some copies and be prepared to accept payment. 
General guidelines: 

Hate speech of any kind is never allowed and will be shut down.
Violence or references to physical harm to others will be shut down.

BYOB is welcome, and some light snacks and drinks are served. 
Accessibility: The Space is located on the second floor of a historic building, accessible via a flight of stairs. Unfortunately, there is no elevator access at this time. This means we are unable to accommodate wheelchairs or guests with significant mobility challenges. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.

title: Exile, Memory, and the Meaning of Home: A Conversation with Ana Hebra Flaster
description:
What happens when the country you love forces you out, leaving you just 48 hours to abandon everything you’ve ever known? Join us online for an extraordinary online conversation with author and essayist Ana Hebra Flaster as we discuss her sweeping yet deeply intimate memoir Property of the Revolution: From a Cuban Barrio to a New Hampshire Mill Town.

Ana Hebra Flaster was six years old when her working-class family was kicked out of their Havana barrio for opposing communism. Once devoted revolutionaries themselves but disillusioned by the Castro government’s repressive tactics, they fled to the US. The permanent losses they suffered—of home, country, and loved ones, all within forty-eight hours—haunted her multigenerational family as they reclaimed their lives and freedom in 1967 New Hampshire. There, they fed each other stories of their scrappy barrio—some of which Hebra Flaster has shared on All Things Considered—to resurrect their lost world and fortify themselves for a daunting task: building a new life in a foreign land.

Weaving pivotal events in Cuba–US history with her viejos’—elders’—stories of surviving political upheaval, impossible choices, and “refugeedom,” Property of the Revolution celebrates the indomitable spirit and wisdom of the women warriors who led the family out of Cuba, shaped its rebirth as Cuban Americans, and helped Ana grow up hopeful, future-facing—American. But what happens when deeply buried childhood memories resurface, demanding an adult’s reckoning?

Here’s how the fiercest love, the most stubborn will, and the power of family put nine new Americans back on their feet.

Register today to gain a deeper, more personal perspective on the refugee experience and the enduring quest to define home.

 

About the Author: 

Ana Hebra Flaster is journalist and the author of Property of the Revolution: From a Cuban Barrio to a New Hampshire Mill Town, published in April 2025 (She Writes Press, Simon and Schuster distribution). A former child-refugee from Cuba, Ana’s work has appeared in national print and online media, including: The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Post, and The Boston Globe. Her commentaries and storytelling have aired on NPR’s All Things Considered and PBS’s Stories from the Stage. Since its publication in April 2025, Property of the Revolution has won first place in several international writing contests, including: 2026 IBPA Book Awards (Memoir); 2025 Discovery Book Awards (Nonfiction overall); 2025 International Book Awards (Creative Nonfiction), and the 2025 IAP Book Awards (Memoir of the Year). The memoir was selected as the Nashua, New Hampshire, 2026 All-City Read and the Rivier University 2025 First-Year Read. title: Library Speakers Consortium - Exile, Memory, and the Meaning of Home: A Conversation with Ana Hebra Flaster
description:
You must register here to attend:  https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/225105



What happens when the country you love forces you out, leaving you just 48 hours to abandon everything you’ve ever known? Join us online for an extraordinary online conversation with author and essayist Ana Hebra Flaster as we discuss her sweeping yet deeply intimate memoir Property of the Revolution: From a Cuban Barrio to a New Hampshire Mill Town.

Ana Hebra Flaster was six years old when her working-class family was kicked out of their Havana barrio for opposing communism. Once devoted revolutionaries themselves but disillusioned by the Castro government’s repressive tactics, they fled to the US. The permanent losses they suffered—of home, country, and loved ones, all within forty-eight hours—haunted her multigenerational family as they reclaimed their lives and freedom in 1967 New Hampshire. There, they fed each other stories of their scrappy barrio—some of which Hebra Flaster has shared on All Things Considered—to resurrect their lost world and fortify themselves for a daunting task: building a new life in a foreign land.

Weaving pivotal events in Cuba–US history with her viejos’—elders’—stories of surviving political upheaval, impossible choices, and “refugeedom,” Property of the Revolution celebrates the indomitable spirit and wisdom of the women warriors who led the family out of Cuba, shaped its rebirth as Cuban Americans, and helped Ana grow up hopeful, future-facing—American. But what happens when deeply buried childhood memories resurface, demanding an adult’s reckoning?

Here’s how the fiercest love, the most stubborn will, and the power of family put nine new Americans back on their feet.

Register today to gain a deeper, more personal perspective on the refugee experience and the enduring quest to define home.

About the Author: 

Ana Hebra Flaster is journalist and the author of Property of the Revolution: From a Cuban Barrio to a New Hampshire Mill Town, published in April 2025 (She Writes Press, Simon and Schuster distribution). A former child-refugee from Cuba, Ana’s work has appeared in national print and online media, including: The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Post, and The Boston Globe. Her commentaries and storytelling have aired on NPR’s All Things Considered and PBS’s Stories from the Stage. Since its publication in April 2025, Property of the Revolution has won first place in several international writing contests, including: 2026 IBPA Book Awards (Memoir); 2025 Discovery Book Awards (Nonfiction overall); 2025 International Book Awards (Creative Nonfiction), and the 2025 IAP Book Awards (Memoir of the Year). The memoir was selected as the Nashua, New Hampshire, 2026 All-City Read and the Rivier University 2025 First-Year Read. Ana speaks regularly with student, library, and civic groups about her family’s journey and the refugee and immigrant experience. She is currently focused on covering the struggle for democracy and human rights in Cuba in her weekly Substack, CubaCurious, a project she launched in July 2024.

title: Comic Strips and Kimchi: Cooking Korean Food Made Easy with Robin Ha
description:
Cooking authentic Korean food at home doesn't have to be intimidating or complicated—in fact, it can be as fun and engaging as reading your favorite graphic novel! Join us for a virtual conversation with artist and author Robin Ha as we explore her New York Times bestselling book, Cook Korean!: A Comic Book Cookbook.

Fun to look at and easy to use, this unique combination of cookbook and graphic novel is the ideal introduction to cooking Korean cuisine at home. Robin Ha’s colorful and humorous one-to three-page comics fully illustrate the steps and ingredients needed to bring more than sixty traditional (and some not-so-traditional) dishes to life.

In these playful but exact recipes, you’ll learn how to create everything from easy kimchi (mak kimchi) and soy garlic beef over rice (bulgogi dupbap) to seaweed rice rolls (gimbap) and beyond. Friendly and inviting, Cook Korean! is perfect for beginners and seasoned cooks alike.

Each chapter includes personal anecdotes and cultural insights from Ha, providing an intimate entry point for those looking to try their hand at this cuisine.

Register today to discover how easy, approachable, and fun authentic Korean cooking can be!

 

About the Author: 

Robin Ha is the New York Times bestselling author and illustrator of Cook Korean!: A Comic Book with Recipes, as well as the graphic novel memoir Almost American Girl and historical fantasy graphic novel The Fox Maidens. Her comics and illustrations have also appeared in various publications, including The Washington Post and The Los Angeles Times, as well as in anthologies highlighting Asian American culture: Rise: A Pop History of Asian America from the Nineties to Now, New Frontiers: The Many Worlds of George Takei, and Shattered: The Asian American Comics Anthology (Secret Identities). Robin grew up reading and drawing comics. At fourteen she moved to the United States from Seoul, Korea. She studied illustration at Rhode Island School of Design. She now lives in Virginia.

description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.
